questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment

options.text: Modify the list of Accepted Domains in the Exchange Online admin center.
Modify the Email integration options in the Org-wide Teams settings in the Microsoft Teams admin center.
Modify the Org-wide Guest access settings in the Microsoft Teams admin center.
Modify the Organization options in the Org-wide Teams settings in the Microsoft Teams admin center.

questions.explanation: Email integration is configured in the Teams Admin Center under Org-wide Teams Settings > Email integration, where you can specify which SMTP domains are allowed to send emails to team channels. This setting applies organization-wide to all teams. Exchange Accepted Domains, Guest access settings, and other organization options do not control channel email permissions.

You need to configure the user accounts of the sales department users to meet the security requirements.  

What should you do for each user?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, set the Microsoft Teams upgrade policy to Skype for Business with Teams collaboration and meetings coexistence mode.
From PowerShell, run the Grant-CsTeamsUpgradePolicy -PolicyName SfBWithTeamsCollab cmdlet.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, set the Microsoft Teams upgrade policy to Skype for Business only coexistence mode.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, set the Microsoft Teams upgrade policy to Skype for Business with Teams collaboration coexistence mode.

questions.explanation: The requirement (from the referenced scenario) is for on-premises Skype for Business to be used for IM and calling only, meaning collaboration and meetings must be handled in Teams. That maps to the Skype for Business with Teams collaboration and meetings coexistence mode, applied via a Microsoft Teams upgrade policy in the Teams admin center — the policy can still be scoped to just the sales department users through the admin center's per-user policy assignment, so a PowerShell cmdlet targeting the narrower SfBWithTeamsCollab policy is unnecessary and would omit the required meetings migration to Teams.

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
Your company has a Microsoft 365 subscription that contains a team named Sales.  

You need to recommend a solution to ensure that all guest users who are members of Sales receive an email message each year to verify that they want to remain in the team.  

What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation: Access Reviews are specifically designed to periodically verify membership in groups and teams. When configured with annual recurrence, they send emails to designated reviewers (or guests themselves) requesting confirmation that members should retain access. This is the recommended solution for annual guest verification in Teams. Identity providers, Outlook add-ins, and communication compliance policies serve different purposes.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
Your company has a Microsoft 365 subscription that contains a team named Sales.  

You need to recommend a solution to ensure that all guest users who are members of Sales receive an email message each year to verify that they want to remain in the team.  

What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: From Guest access in the Org-wide settings, set Allow guest access in Microsoft Teams to On.
Edit the Meeting settings and set Anonymous users can join a meeting to On.
Edit the global meeting policy and set Allow scheduling private meetings to On.
Edit the live events policy and set Who can join live events to Everyone.

questions.explanation:
In Microsoft Teams, users who join a meeting without signing in with a work or school account (such as external users invited via an Outlook meeting link) are considered anonymous users. By default, this capability can be disabled, preventing such users from joining. To allow external/anonymous users to join Teams meetings, an administrator must go to Meeting settings in the Teams admin center and turn on 'Anonymous users can join a meeting.' Guest access settings instead control whether external users can be added as guests to teams and channels for persistent collaboration, which is a different scenario from simply joining a scheduled meeting.

**Learn more:** [Allow anonymous users to join meetings - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-cloud-video-interop-plan#allow-anonymous-users-to-join-meetings) · [Meeting settings in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/meeting-settings-in-teams)

Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription containing 20 teams. You need to make sure that a team named Team1 is displayed as Highly Confidential within the Microsoft Teams client. What should you use?

options.text: a teams app setup policy in the Microsoft Teams admin center
a sensitivity label in the Microsoft 365 Compliance admin center
a supervision policy in the Microsoft 365 Compliance admin center
a teams policy in the Microsoft Teams admin center

questions.explanation:
Sensitivity labels, created and published from the Microsoft Purview compliance portal (Microsoft 365 Compliance admin center), can be applied to Microsoft 365 groups and sites, including Teams. When you configure the label's Groups & sites scope, you can set a classification name — such as 'Highly Confidential' — that is displayed to end users as a visual marking in the Teams client, letting members immediately see the sensitivity classification of that team. This capability is unique to sensitivity labels; Teams app setup policies control which apps are pinned or available, Teams policies govern general Teams feature behavior, and supervision policies are used for compliance-based communication monitoring, none of which display a classification marking on a team.

**Learn more:** [Sensitivity labels for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/sensitivity-labels) · [Use sensitivity labels to protect collaborative workspaces (groups and sites)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a Microsoft 365 subscription.  

You have a team that uses the following dynamic rule.  

(user.department -contains "Sales" -or user.department  

-contains "Marketing") -and (user.userType -Contains "Guest")  

-and (user.country -eq "US")  

Which user will be included in the group?

options.text: A guest user in a department named Global Sales that has the country attribute set to US.
A member user in a department named Marketing Division that has the country attribute set to US.
A member user in a department named Marketing/Sales that has the country attribute set to US.
A guest user in a department named US Marketing Division that has the country attribute set to US.

questions.explanation: The dynamic rule requires (Sales OR Marketing) AND Guest AND country=US. Option D (guest user in 'US Marketing Division', country US) matches all three conditions: department contains 'Marketing', user type is guest, and country is US. Options B and C fail the guest requirement; A also matches but D is the consensus answer.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes a Microsoft Teams auto attendant. Calls made to the auto attendant will be redirected to a shared voicemail.  
  
You need to create a group to use for this shared voicemail.  
  
Which type of group should you create?
questions.explanation:
Shared voicemail in Teams is delivered to a group's mailbox/associated folder, and the group used for this purpose must be a Microsoft 365 group, since it provides the mailbox and (optionally) Teams channel needed to store and surface shared voicemail messages for auto attendants and call queues. A plain security group has no mailbox and cannot be used for this purpose. (Microsoft has since also enabled distribution lists and mail-enabled security groups as alternate options, but delivers each user an individual copy rather than storing it in a shared group folder, and the certified/documented answer for this scenario is the Microsoft 365 group.) See Microsoft's documentation on managing shared voicemail for Teams auto attendants and call queues.

**Learn more:** [Manage Shared Voicemail - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-shared-voicemail) · [Exam MS-700 topic 4 question 16 discussion - ExamTopics](https://www.examtopics.com/discussions/microsoft/view/43904-exam-ms-700-topic-4-question-16-discussion/)

Your company has a Microsoft 365 subscription. You need to create an auto attendant from the Microsoft Teams admin center. Which object must be associated to the auto attendant?
questions.explanation:
When you create an auto attendant in the Teams admin center, it must be associated with a resource account. The resource account represents the auto attendant as an identity in Microsoft 365, must be assigned a Microsoft Teams Phone Resource Account license, and (for a first-level auto attendant that callers dial directly) is assigned the service telephone number used to reach the auto attendant. Without an associated resource account, the auto attendant cannot be reached by callers or properly function within Teams Phone System. A conferencing bridge, shared mailbox, and Calling Plan are unrelated or optional components, not the mandatory object that must be linked to the auto attendant itself.

**Learn more:** [Setup - Auto Attendant - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/aa-cq-setup-auto-attendant) · [Manage - Resource accounts for Teams Phone Agent, Auto attendants and Call Queue - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/aa-cq-manage-resource-accounts)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network contains an Active Directory domain. The domain contains 1,000 computers that run Windows 11.  
  
Your company uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
You need to ensure that the computers can prioritize audio and video during Teams meetings.  
  
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, you set Insert Quality of Service (QoS) markers for real-time media traffic to On.  
  
What should you do next?

options.text: From Meeting settings in the Microsoft Teams admin center, configure the media port range to use any available ports.
From Group Policy Management, create a Group Policy setting to specify the DSCP values.
From the Teams PowerShell module, create a network roaming policy.
From Meeting policies in the Microsoft Teams admin center, configure the Media bit rate (Kbs) setting.

questions.explanation: After enabling 'Insert QoS markers' in the Microsoft Teams admin center, computers must be configured to recognize and prioritize these DSCP markings. Group Policy settings in the Active Directory domain specify DSCP values and associated priority queues for different traffic types. This allows network routers and endpoints to identify Teams audio/video packets and treat them as high-priority traffic.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has a subscription to Microsoft 365.  

All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E5 license.  

A user named User1 has the Microsoft Teams desktop client on his Windows 10 client computer.  

User1 reports several problems when using Microsoft Teams.  

You need to view the debug logs on User1's computer.  

Which of the following actions should you perform to generate the debug logs?

options.text: Press the following key combination: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+1.
Right click on the Teams icon and select Get Logs.
Use Windows Event Viewer and browse to the Application Log.
Run a Usage report in the Teams admin center.

questions.explanation: The keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Alt+Shift+1 is the official Microsoft method to generate debug logs in the Teams desktop client on Windows. This opens a log collection dialog and stores logs in the user's Downloads folder. Right-clicking Teams and selecting 'Get Logs' is an alternative method, but the keyboard shortcut is the more direct administrative approach. Event Viewer and admin reports do not provide Teams-specific debug logs.

You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has recently purchased a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in your company have a  

Microsoft 365 E3 license.  

You are in the process of configuring Microsoft Teams.  

You need to restrict the companies that users can communicate with to five supplier companies. You have a list of email domains used by the supplier companies.  

Which of the following actions should you configure?
questions.explanation: External access settings allow administrators to create an allowlist of specific email domains for federated communication. By configuring external access to allow only the five supplier company domains, administrators restrict Teams users to communicate exclusively with those verified partner organizations.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment

options.text: the External collaboration settings in the Azure Active Directory admin center
the list of accepted domains in Microsoft Exchange Online

questions.explanation:
Restricting which external senders can email a Teams channel is configured in the Microsoft Teams admin center under Org-wide settings > Teams settings, in the Email integration section, using the 'Accept channel email from these SMTP domains' option. By default Teams accepts channel email from any domain; changing this setting to a specific allow list (which can include the internal domain plus fabrikam.com) restricts channel email to only those specified domains, satisfying the requirement that only internal users and @fabrikam.com addresses can send email to team channels.

**Learn more:** [Teams settings and policies reference - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/settings-policies-reference) · [How to Control Sending Email to Teams Channels | Practical365](https://practical365.com/how-to-control-sending-email-to-teams-channels/)

Solution: From a team, add a tab for the Sales site.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
A SharePoint tab merely pins SharePoint content in a Teams channel; it does not make Sales the team-connected SharePoint site. A team connected to a SharePoint site stores each standard channel’s files in a corresponding folder in that parent site’s default document library. Connecting an existing SharePoint site to a team requires adding Teams to that site (or creating a team from its associated Microsoft 365 group).\
\
**Learn more:** [Teams and SharePoint integration - SharePoint in Microsoft 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/teams-connected-sites)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Teams client, create a new team and choose **Create from an existing Office 365 group or team**.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
A team created from an existing Microsoft 365 group is connected to that group’s associated SharePoint site. Standard-channel files are stored in channel-specific folders in the parent site’s default document library, so new standard channels create corresponding folders in the Sales site.\
\
**Learn more:** [Teams and SharePoint integration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/teams-connected-sites) · [Microsoft 365 Groups and Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/office-365-groups)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
Solution: From the Sales site, select the **Create a Team** option.  
  
Does this fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation:
Adding Teams to an existing SharePoint site connects that site to the new team. Each standard channel’s Files tab is connected to a folder in the parent site’s default document library, so standard channels added to the team create their associated folders in the Sales site.\
\
**Learn more:** [Teams and SharePoint integration - SharePoint in Microsoft 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/teams-connected-sites)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: From the Sales site, select the **Create a Team** option.  
  
Does this fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation:
`Set-AzureADGroup` changes Microsoft Entra ID group properties; it does not associate an existing SharePoint site with a Microsoft 365 group and Teams. A Teams-connected group must use the corresponding SharePoint team site so that creating channels provisions their folders in that site's document library. The SharePoint Online `Set-SPOSiteOffice365Group` cmdlet is the cmdlet that connects an existing top-level site collection to a new Microsoft 365 group. [Set-SPOSiteOffice365Group — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.online.sharepoint.powershell/set-spositeoffice365group?view=sharepoint-ps)

**Learn more:** [Set-SPOSiteOffice365Group — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.online.sharepoint.powershell/set-spositeoffice365group?view=sharepoint-ps)

questions.question:
Solution: From the Sales site, you select the **Add Microsoft Teams** link.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Adding Teams to an existing SharePoint site connects that site to the new team. Each standard channel’s Files tab is associated with a folder in the parent SharePoint site’s default document library, so new standard channels have folders created in the Sales site.\
\
**Learn more:** [Teams and SharePoint integration - SharePoint in Microsoft 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/teams-connected-sites)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Teams client, create a new team and choose **From a group or team**.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
A team created from an existing Microsoft 365 group connects to the SharePoint site associated with that group. Standard Teams channels use separate folders in the parent SharePoint site’s default document library, so new standard channels create their corresponding folders in the Sales site.\
\
**Learn more:** [Overview of Teams and SharePoint integration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/teams-connected-sites) · [Overview of teams and channels in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-channels-overview)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Teams.  
  
A user named User1 reports that the recording button is unavailable during a Teams meeting.  
  
You need to ensure that the recording button is available for User1.  
  
What should you configure in the Microsoft Teams admin center?
questions.explanation:
Whether a user sees the Record button in a meeting is governed by the Meeting recording setting inside a Teams meeting policy assigned to that user (or the Global policy). Meeting settings controls tenant-wide meeting engagement options such as anonymous join, not per-user recording rights, and meeting templates/template policies only control which meeting experience (webinar, town hall, etc.) is offered.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage meeting recording policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/meeting-recording)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Teams deployment.  
  
All users are assigned Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses.  
  
You need to ensure that Teams meeting participants can access Copilot features during and after a meeting.  
  
Which setting should you enable first?

options.text: Require participant agreement for recording and transcription

questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams meetings relies on meeting transcripts to generate summaries and insights both during and after meetings. Enabling transcription is the prerequisite setting that allows Copilot to access the meeting content needed for its analysis features.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
Your company uses Teams.  
  
A user reports that when they manually decline a Teams call, the call is NOT sent to their Teams voicemail.  
  
Which setting should you configure?

options.text: Busy on busy when in a call

questions.explanation: A user's personal call-answering behavior, including what happens to a call that is declined or goes unanswered, is governed by the Calls ring me setting and its \"If unanswered\" option. If that option is left at its default rather than set to voicemail, a manually declined call simply ends instead of being routed to the user's mailbox, so an administrator or the user must configure Calls ring me to send those calls to voicemail.

You have a Microsoft 365 subscription and a Teams Phone deployment.  
  
You purchase 50 certified Teams devices to be used as common area phones.  
  
To the subscription, you upload a file that contains the MAC address of each device.  
  
You need to ensure that field technicians can provision each device.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation: After uploading a file of device MAC addresses to the Teams admin center, the admin generates verification codes for each device; field technicians then enter the device-specific verification code directly on the phone to complete sign-in without needing user credentials. App setup policies, IP Phone policies, and configuration profiles govern app pinning and device settings after sign-in, not the initial unattended provisioning workflow. **Learn more:** [Remote provisioning and sign in for Teams phones](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/phones/remote-provision-remote-login-phones)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization uses Microsoft 365, and you recently configured the company's Microsoft Teams upgrade policy to use Teams only coexistence mode.  
  
A user reports that several of their online meetings are still configured to use Microsoft Skype for Business.  
  
You need to convert the online meetings on this user's calendar so that they use Microsoft Teams instead.  
  
What are two possible ways to accomplish this goal? (Each correct answer presents a complete solution. Choose two.)

options.text: From PowerShell, run the Start-CsExMeetingMigration cmdlet and specify the -identity parameter.
Run the Skype for Business Meeting Migration tool.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the meeting policy.
From PowerShell, run the Set-CsTeamsUpgradeConfiguration cmdlet.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the Microsoft Teams upgrade policy.

questions.explanation:
Converting existing Skype for Business meeting invitations on a user's calendar to Teams meetings requires the Meeting Migration Service (MMS) functionality, not changes to upgrade or meeting policies. An administrator can manually trigger this for a specific user by running the Start-CsExMeetingMigration cmdlet with the -Identity parameter, which queues a migration request that updates the meeting join information from Skype for Business to Teams. Alternatively, the Skype for Business Meeting Migration Tool can be run to update the user's existing meeting invites to Teams meetings. Modifying the Teams upgrade policy or running Set-CsTeamsUpgradeConfiguration only affects how the tenant/user is upgraded to TeamsOnly mode going forward, and modifying meeting policies affects meeting feature behavior — neither converts already-scheduled Skype for Business meeting items to Teams meetings.

**Learn more:** [Start-CsExMeetingMigration (MicrosoftTeams) | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/start-csexmeetingmigration?view=teams-ps) · [Using the Meeting Migration Service (MMS) - Skype for Business Online | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/skypeforbusiness/audio-conferencing-in-office-365/setting-up-the-meeting-migration-service-mms)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has a main office in New York and 20 branch offices in North America. Some of the branch offices are in locations with low bandwidth Internet connectivity.  

The company has a Microsoft 365 subscription. All users in the company have a Microsoft 365 E3 license.  

All users in the main office use Microsoft Teams for collaboration.  

You want to roll out Microsoft Teams to all branch office users. However, you are concerned about the branch offices Internet connectivity. You need to verify that the branch offices have enough bandwidth to support audio and video conferencing using Microsoft Teams.  

Which of the following should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Teams Network Planner is purpose-built to estimate the bandwidth a location needs to support Teams audio, video, and screen-sharing based on the number of users and expected usage patterns, making it the right tool to assess whether low-bandwidth branch offices can support Teams calling before rollout. The Call Quality Dashboard and Network Monitor are used after deployment to analyze actual call quality or capture packets, not to plan bandwidth requirements up front.

**Learn more:** [Use Network Planner for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/network-planner)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in the company have a Microsoft 365 E3 license.  

All users use Microsoft Skype for Business Online for collaboration.  

You plan to migrate all users to Microsoft Teams.  

You need to ensure that users can use both Microsoft Skype for Business Online and Microsoft Teams during the migration period.  

You need to configure the Teams upgrade settings to ensure that users receive chats and calls in Skype for Business but use Microsoft Teams for group collaboration and meeting scheduling.  

Which of the following coexistence modes should you configure?

options.text: Skype for Business with Teams collaboration
Skype for Business with Teams collaboration and meetings

questions.explanation: The 'Skype for Business with Teams collaboration and meetings' coexistence mode allows users to receive chats and calls via Skype for Business while using Teams exclusively for group collaboration (channels) and meeting scheduling. This is the recommended mode during mid-migration when maintaining backward compatibility with Skype for Business clients. Islands mode allows parallel use of both clients independently.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to create a team for the sales department.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a team and modify the membership rule for the team's Office 365 group.
From PowerShell, run the Add-AzureAdGroupMember cmdlet.
From PowerShell, run the New-Team cmdlet.
Create a team and select Build a team from scratch.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams does not expose an option to create a team with dynamic membership directly from the Teams client or from the New-Team cmdlet. Dynamic membership rules are a feature of Azure AD groups, so the correct process is to first create the team (which creates its associated Office 365 group), and then edit that group's membership type and rule in Azure AD to make it dynamic. This is documented under Azure AD dynamic group membership rules, which apply to Microsoft 365 groups used by Teams.

**Learn more:** [Create a dynamic group and check status - Azure Active Directory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/enterprise-users/groups-create-rule)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams and contains a user named User1. User1 has a Windows 10 device that has the Teams desktop client installed.  
  
The Teams desktop client has the notification settings shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783721430829-djhnp3z8.png)  
  
User1 reports that he does NOT receive alerts for Teams activities on his device.  
  
What should you do to ensure that User1 receives Teams alerts?

options.text: From the Settings app, modify the Focus assist settings.
From the Microsoft Teams client change Teams and channels notifications to All activity.
From the Settings app, modify the Notifications & actions settings.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the Messaging policies settings.

questions.explanation: The exhibit shows that the Teams client's own notification settings are already configured to alert the user, so the app itself is not the cause. On a Windows 10 device, the operating system separately controls whether an app is allowed to raise notifications at all, and if Microsoft Teams is blocked or disabled under Notifications & actions, no banners or alerts reach the user regardless of the in-app configuration. Focus assist would only suppress alerts during specific priority or automatic-rule periods, not block them entirely.

questions.explanation:
Global Reader is a Microsoft 365 admin role that provides read-only access to administrative settings and reports across almost all Microsoft 365 admin centers, including the Teams admin center's Analytics & reports section, without granting any configuration or management rights. This satisfies the least-privilege requirement, unlike Skype for Business Administrator (full management rights over Teams/Skype settings) or Global Administrator (full tenant control), and unlike Teams Communications Support Specialist, which only allows viewing per-user call analytics for troubleshooting rather than the full Analytics & reports view.

**Learn more:** [Use Microsoft Teams administrator roles to manage Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/using-admin-roles) · [About Microsoft 365 admin roles - Global Reader](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/add-users/about-admin-roles)

questions.question:
Your company uses Microsoft Teams.  

The company has the departments and teams shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783720575655-656ff14i.png)  
  
You need to recommend a solution to prevent the users in each department from inviting users from other departments to their team.  

What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation: Information barrier policies prevent users in different segments or departments from collaborating. They block adding users to teams across boundaries, prevent access to team/channel content across barriers, and restrict 1:1 and group chats between segmented users. This is the specific solution designed to prevent cross-departmental collaboration in Microsoft Teams.

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, you review the Microsoft Call Quality Dashboard.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Call Quality Dashboard provides organization-wide call-quality reports and includes packet loss rate and packet-loss-related measures for Teams media streams, allowing network packet loss during calls to be identified.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Call Quality Dashboard (CQD)?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/cqd-what-is-call-quality-dashboard) · [Dimensions and measurements available in Call Quality Dashboard](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/dimensions-and-measures-available-in-call-quality-dashboard)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
Solution: You run the Network Testing Companion.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Network Testing Companion assesses network readiness through tests rather than reporting packet-loss data from live Teams calls. Teams call-quality telemetry records packet loss for actual sessions and is available through the Teams admin center troubleshooting experience and Call Quality Dashboard.\
\
**Learn more:** [Monitor and troubleshoot Teams meetings and calls from the Teams admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/monitor-troubleshoot-teams-meetings-calls) · [Use CQD to manage call and meeting quality in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/quality-of-experience-review-guide)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, you choose **Analytics & reports**.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Packet-loss information is exposed in Teams call-quality telemetry, including the Call Quality Dashboard. The Teams admin center navigation path requires selecting **Analytics & reports > Call Quality Dashboard**; opening only **Analytics & reports** does not identify packet loss for calls.\
\
**Learn more:** [Call Quality Dashboard (CQD) setup - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/turning-on-and-using-call-quality-dashboard) · [Monitor and troubleshoot Teams meetings and calls from the Teams admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/monitor-troubleshoot-teams-meetings-calls)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
Solution: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, you run the Network Planner.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Network Planner calculates bandwidth and network requirements for a Teams deployment based on network details and expected usage; it does not measure packet loss during actual calls. Teams call-quality tools provide the call telemetry used to identify packet loss.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use the Network planner for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/network-planner) · [Monitor and improve call quality for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/monitor-call-quality-qos)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, review **Usage reports**.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Teams Usage reports measure user activity and adoption rather than call-media network telemetry. Packet loss is a call-quality metric; it is investigated through Teams call analytics for individual calls or through Call Quality Dashboard for organization-wide analysis.\
\
**Learn more:** [Monitor and improve call quality for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/monitor-call-quality-qos) · [Monitor and troubleshoot Teams meetings and calls from the Teams admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/monitor-troubleshoot-teams-meetings-calls)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that contains an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment. The Azure Virtual Desktop deployment contains a session host named Host.  
  
You install the Remote Desktop WebRTC Redirector Service and the Teams for virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) client on Host.  
  
You need to configure the WebRTC Redirector Service to only support content sharing from an application window.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution,  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Set the DisableRAILScreensharing registry key value to 1.
Set the UseHardwareEncoding registry key value to 1.
Set the ShareClientDesktop registry key value to 0.
Set the ShareClientDesktop registry key value to 1.
Set the DisableRAILAppSharing registry key value to 1.

questions.explanation:
Enabling content sharing for classic Teams as a RemoteApp on Azure Virtual Desktop first requires ShareClientDesktop set to 1, which turns the feature on; DisableRAILScreensharing must then be set to 1 to turn off full-desktop sharing while leaving application-window sharing available (Microsoft's documentation explicitly notes ShareClientDesktop must be enabled before this key takes effect). DisableRAILAppSharing does the opposite (removes window sharing instead), and UseHardwareEncoding only affects outgoing camera video quality, not content sharing scope.

**Learn more:** [Use Microsoft Teams on Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/teams-on-avd)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You plan to use Teams.  
  
You run the Microsoft 365 network connectivity test tool and generate a report.  
  
You discover that the Microsoft Teams section of the report has a warning notification for media connectivity.  
  
You suspect a firewall issue at the test location.  
  
Which destination protocol and port range should you configure on the firewall?
questions.explanation: Teams media connectivity uses UDP ports 3478 through 3481 for STUN/TURN and media relay operations. TCP ports are not used for media streaming; those are used for signaling and other control traffic. The port range 50020-50059 and 50000-50019 are not standard Teams ports.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You plan to use Teams.  
  
You run the Microsoft 365 network connectivity test tool and generate a report.  
  
You discover that the Microsoft Teams section of the report has a warning notification for media connectivity.  
  
You suspect a firewall issue at the test location.  
  
Which destination protocol and port range should you configure on the firewall?
questions.explanation:
A network roaming policy lets you assign bandwidth and video settings to a specific network site, so the restriction is applied dynamically only when a user's Teams client detects it is connected from that site, such as the branch office; a meeting policy supplies the actual media bit-rate and video values that get enforced. Calling, voice routing, and Audio Conferencing routing policies govern call routing and PSTN behavior, not location-based bandwidth enforcement.

**Learn more:** [Network roaming policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/network-roaming-policy)

You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams and contains a user named User1.  

User1 reports that the Meeting recording button is missing from the Microsoft Teams client. The user cannot record meetings.  

You need to ensure that User1 meets the prerequisites to record Microsoft Teams meetings.  

What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, use the Call Quality Dashboard (CQD).
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, use Teams advisor.
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, enter Diag: Missing Recording in the Need help? search box.
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, enter Diag: Meeting Recording in the Need help? search box.

questions.explanation: The Microsoft 365 admin center diagnostic tool 'Diag: Meeting Recording' specifically troubleshoots meeting recording prerequisites and issues. Entering this diagnostic search will identify whether User1 has the necessary prerequisites (license, policy settings, storage) to enable the recording button in Teams meetings.

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization's Microsoft 365 subscription includes three groups: HR, Marketing, and Sales.  
  
You must configure the Microsoft Teams desktop client so that the solution satisfies these requirements:  
  
- HR group members must be prevented from pinning apps to their app bar.  
- Marketing group members must have the Microsoft Planner app pinned to their app bar.  
- Sales group members must remain unaffected by any policies applied to the Marketing and HR groups.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Modify the global app setup policy.
Modify the global app permission policy.
Create an app setup policy for HR.
Create an app setup policy for Marketing.
Create an app permission policy for Marketing.
Create an app permission policy for HR.

questions.explanation:
App setup policies govern the app bar experience in Teams — which apps are pinned and whether users are allowed to pin their own apps (via the 'User pinning' setting). Creating a dedicated app setup policy for HR with user pinning disabled prevents HR members from pinning apps, and creating a dedicated app setup policy for Marketing that includes Planner in its pinned apps list ensures Planner is pinned for that group. Because custom policies only apply to the users/groups they are explicitly assigned to, and the Global (Org-wide default) app setup policy continues to apply to everyone else, leaving the Global policy unmodified ensures Sales remains unaffected. App permission policies control which apps can be installed or are blocked — they do not control pinning or the app bar layout — so they are not the mechanism needed here.

**Learn more:** [Manage agents and app setup policies in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-app-setup-policies) · [Overview of app policies to manage apps in Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/app-policies)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to configure the environment so that it satisfies the security requirements related to team names.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft 365 Compliance admin center, create a sensitivity label and a sensitivity policy.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the Teams setting policies.
From the Azure Active Directory admin center, upload a blocked word list for the group naming policy.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams team names are built on Microsoft 365 Groups, so any policy restricting or blocking specific words in team names must be configured through the Microsoft 365 Groups naming policy in the Azure Active Directory (Microsoft Entra ID) admin center. This naming policy supports uploading a custom blocked words list (a CSV of comma-separated phrases), which prevents users from including those words in group/team names and aliases. When a user tries to use a blocked word while naming a team, Microsoft Teams displays an error identifying the blocked word so the user must remove it before the team can be created. The Microsoft 365 Compliance admin center (sensitivity labels/policies) governs information protection and labeling, not name text validation, and the Microsoft Teams admin center's Teams settings policies control app/feature behavior, not naming restrictions—neither can enforce blocked words in team names.

**Learn more:** [Enforce a group naming policy in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-naming-policy) · [Microsoft 365 Groups and Microsoft Teams naming policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/solutions/groups-naming-policy?view=o365-worldwide)

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company uses Microsoft Teams.  

All the teams used by the company's legal department must meet the following compliance requirements:  

✑ Each team must expire 365 days after it is created.  

✑ All team content must be deleted when the team expires.  

✑ An administrator must be able to restore deleted team content for 30 days.  

What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft 365 compliance center, create a retention policy.
From the Azure Active Directory admin center, configure Microsoft 365 Groups expiration.
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, modify the Office 365 group settings.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the team's policy.

questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 Groups expiration policy in Azure Active Directory configures team expiration after 365 days, automatic content deletion when teams expire, and the 30-day soft-delete retention period allowing administrator restoration. This policy addresses all three compliance requirements for Teams used by the legal department.

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a Microsoft 365 subscription. The subscription contains 200 Microsoft Teams users and a team named IT Support that has 50 members.  
  
You need to ensure that the caller ID for outbound PSTN calls from IT Support is the phone number of the company's IT helpdesk. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
Which two tools should you include in the solution? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: the Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) PowerShell for Graph module
the Skype for Business admin center

questions.explanation: To set caller ID for outbound PSTN calls from a specific team, you need the Microsoft Teams PowerShell module (for configuration cmdlets like Set-CsCallingLineIdentity) and the Skype for Business admin center (for managing caller ID policies). These two tools together provide the necessary configuration capabilities for team-level caller ID assignment while minimizing administrative overhead.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Systems Administrator for your company, which has a Microsoft 365 subscription. All users in the company have a Microsoft 365 E3 license.  
  
You have been migrating users from Microsoft Skype for Business Online to Microsoft Teams over the last two months, and most users are now using Microsoft Teams. The coexistence mode is currently set to Islands.  
  
You plan to change the coexistence mode to Teams Only to force all users to use Microsoft Teams.  
  
You need to ensure that if any users have online meetings scheduled to use Skype for Business, those meetings are converted to use Microsoft Teams.  
  
Which of the following actions should you perform?

options.text: Modify the default Meeting policy in the Microsoft Teams admin center.

questions.explanation:
The Meeting Migration Service (MMS) is the Microsoft 365 service responsible for converting existing Skype for Business scheduled meetings into Microsoft Teams meetings. This conversion can be manually initiated for a user account with the Start-CsExMeetingMigration cmdlet (for example, using the -TargetMeetingType Teams parameter), which triggers MMS to update the user's meeting invitations so that they use Teams instead of Skype for Business. Set-CsTeamsUpgradeConfiguration only controls tenant-wide upgrade notifications and app download settings during coexistence, not the conversion of individual scheduled meetings. Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration configures meeting invite branding and help URLs, not meeting migration. Modifying the default Meeting policy only affects meeting behavior for future meetings scheduled in Teams, not existing Skype for Business meeting invitations.

**Learn more:** [Start-CsExMeetingMigration (MicrosoftTeams) | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/start-csexmeetingmigration?view=teams-ps) · [Using the Meeting Migration Service (MMS) - Skype for Business Online | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/skypeforbusiness/audio-conferencing-in-office-365/setting-up-the-meeting-migration-service-mms)

Microsoft 365 E3 license.  

All users in the company use Microsoft Teams for collaboration.  

The company has hired a new technician to help with the management of Microsoft Teams.  

You need to assign a security role to the new technician to ensure that he can perform the following tasks for all users:  

✑ Manage meetings, including meeting policies and configurations.  

✑ Manage voice, including calling policies and phone number inventory and assignment.  

Which of the following roles should you assign to the technician? The solution must minimize the assigned permissions.
questions.explanation: The Teams Communications Administrator role has explicit permissions to manage both meetings (including policies and configurations) and voice (including calling policies and phone number inventory). This role provides the minimum permissions necessary for the described tasks without broader administrative access.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Teams.  
  
You have a team named Team1 that contains guest users.  
  
You need to ensure that the members of Team1 are prevented from sharing sensitive information with the guest users during Teams private chats or in Teams channels.  
  
Which type of policy should you configure?
questions.explanation: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies are designed to detect and prevent the sharing of sensitive information automatically, regardless of whether communication is with internal members or guest users. DLP policies examine message content and block sensitive data from being transmitted.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Teams.  
  
You have a team named Team1 that contains guest users.  
  
You need to ensure that the members of Team1 are prevented from sharing sensitive information with the guest users during Teams private chats or in Teams channels.  
  
Which type of policy should you configure?

options.text: For Admin1, run the Grant-CsUserPolicyPackage PowerShell cmdlet.
Assign a Teams Premium license to Admin1.
For Admin1, run the Grant-CsGroupPolicyPackageAssignment PowerShell cmdlet.
Assign a Microsoft 365 E5 license to Admin1.

questions.explanation: Creating and assigning custom policy packages in Teams requires a Teams Premium license. Teams Administrators with standard licenses can only assign default policy packages; custom policy package creation is a premium feature. PowerShell cmdlets and license upgrades to E5 do not enable this capability.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling

options.text: In the global meeting policy, set Who can bypass the lobby to Everyone.
Create a new meeting policy and set Who can bypass the lobby to Everyone.
Apply the policy to the sales department users.
In the global meeting policy, set Who can bypass the lobby to People in my organization.

questions.explanation: Because the requirement must apply only to sales department users, a new (custom) meeting policy with "Who can bypass the lobby" set to Everyone must be created and then assigned specifically to those users; changing the global meeting policy would affect all users in the tenant, not just sales. Setting the global policy's lobby bypass to "People in my organization" would not admit external guests by default at all.

You have a Teams deployment.  
  
A user reports that the Teams client on their Windows device fails to update to the latest release automatically.  
  
What is the cause of the issue?

options.text: The Teams client is installed to a non-default location.
A Teams update policy is misconfigured.
The Teams upgrade settings are misconfigured.

questions.explanation: The Teams desktop client only auto-updates when it is installed to its default per-user location; if it was deployed via a script or MSI to the Program Files folder or another non-default path, the client cannot check for and apply updates automatically. Update and upgrade policies in the Teams admin center govern the new-Teams migration experience, not the classic client's binary self-update mechanism, so they are not the cause here. **Learn more:** [Automatic update not working in Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/microsoftteams/teams-sign-in/teams-doesnt-automatically-update)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes Teams.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to investigate actions that relate to the following Teams activities:  
  
• A new team is created.  

• A new channel is added to a team.  

• A team member changes their role membership.  
  
The solution must ensure that you can specify a start date and end date of the activities.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview Audit (the unified audit log) records Teams activities such as team creation, channel additions, and role membership changes, and lets an investigator filter results by a specific start and end date range. Teams usage reports and Teams advisor provide usage statistics and rollout guidance rather than searchable, dated activity records, and eDiscovery is designed to locate content for legal holds, not to audit administrative or membership actions. **Learn more:** [Audit log activities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-log-activities)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
Your company uses Teams.  
  
You successfully port and assign an audio conferencing toll-free number to Microsoft.  
  
You test the toll-free number and ensure that meetings are successful.  
  
The next day, you receive reports that the toll-free number is no longer working, but local toll numbers still work.  
  
You need to ensure that the toll-free number works.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add the toll-free number to an Audio Conferencing policy.
Set Anonymous users and dial-in callers can start a meeting to On.
Set the toll-free number as the default conference bridge.

questions.explanation: Toll-free numbers require Communication Credits to function—Microsoft bills per-minute for toll-free call usage. The fact that local toll numbers work indicates the number is properly configured; the failure of toll-free numbers specifically points to missing Communication Credits to cover the per-minute charges.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You have a virtualized desktop infrastructure (VDI) that contains the virtual machines shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783712160019-ulkoxtzx.png)  
  
You need to install the Teams for VDI client on supported virtual machines.  
  
Which virtual machines support the Teams for VDI client?
questions.explanation: Teams for VDI is supported only on Windows-based virtual desktop infrastructure platforms including Windows 10 Enterprise multi-session, Windows 11 Enterprise, and Windows Server operating systems. Linux virtual machines (Host4) do not support the Teams VDI client. Therefore, only Host1, Host2, and Host3 support the Teams for VDI client.

options.text: Configure the External access settings in Org-wide settings.
Configure the Teams settings in Org-wide settings.
Configure the Guest access settings in Org-wide settings.
Configure the Audio & Video settings in the default Meeting Policy

questions.explanation: Guest access settings in the Teams admin center (under Org-wide settings) control specific capabilities for guest users, including video conferencing permissions. By disabling the 'Video conferencing' toggle in guest access settings, administrators can prevent guest users from using cameras while keeping the feature enabled for internal users.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Teams with Operator Connect.  
  
You plan to deploy Teams conference phones that support PSTN calls and one-touch join for Teams calendar meetings.  
  
Which license should you assign to each conference phone?
questions.explanation: Conference phones with PSTN calling and one-touch join for Teams meetings require a Teams Rooms Pro license. While the subscription may be Microsoft 365 E5, individual conference phone devices need the Teams Rooms Pro license to enable audio conferencing and automatic meeting join functionality.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Your company uses Teams.  
  
All users are assigned a Microsoft 365 E5 license.  
  
You need to purchase an add-on license that will enable the users to apply a sensitivity label to control the end-to-end encryption of highly sensitive Teams meetings.  
  
Which add-on license should you purchase?
questions.explanation: Teams Premium is the add-on license required for sensitivity labels that enable end-to-end encryption control in Teams meetings. This feature is not included in Microsoft 365 E5 by default and must be purchased separately. Priva, Audio Conferencing, and the E5 Security/Compliance add-ons do not provide this capability.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Your company uses Teams.  
  
All users are assigned a Microsoft 365 E5 license.  
  
You need to purchase an add-on license that will enable the users to apply a sensitivity label to control the end-to-end encryption of highly sensitive Teams meetings.  
  
Which add-on license should you purchase?
questions.explanation: The Teams Communications Support Engineer role has explicit access to advanced troubleshooting toolsets and can monitor call quality using the Call Quality Dashboard down to the individual user level. This role provides the minimum permissions for advanced troubleshooting tasks without broader administrative capabilities.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft 365 tenant.  
  
Guest users report that they cannot access files or Microsoft OneNote from Microsoft Teams, although they can access channels, chats, and conversations without any problem.  
  
You need to ensure that the guest users can access the files and OneNote from Microsoft Teams.  
  
For which service should you configure external sharing?
questions.explanation:
Teams stores channel files and OneNote notebooks in SharePoint Online document libraries (chat files are stored in OneDrive for Business, but the scenario points to files/OneNote accessed through Teams, which are SharePoint-backed). Guest access to that content is governed by the organization-level external sharing policy in the SharePoint admin center. If SharePoint Online sharing is not set to allow new and existing guests (or a more permissive level), guests will still be able to use Teams chat, channels, and conversations—since those are controlled by Azure AD B2B/Teams guest access settings—but they will be blocked from opening the Files tab or OneNote content. Configuring external sharing for SharePoint Online resolves this by permitting the underlying document library and notebook access for guest accounts.

**Learn more:** [Guests can't access Files tab for shared files in Teams - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/microsoftteams/files/guests-cannot-access-files) · [Overview of external sharing in SharePoint and OneDrive in Microsoft 365 - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/external-sharing-overview)

You have a Teams deployment.  
  
You change the display name and profile photo of a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that the changes are displayed as soon as possible in the new Teams client for User1.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Run the Microsoft Support and Recovery Assistant.

questions.explanation: Teams caches user attributes such as display name and photo locally on the client for capacity and performance reasons, so an admin update isn't reflected immediately; to force the new Teams client to pick up the change as soon as possible, the client cache must be cleared (or the user signs out and back in). Running the Support and Recovery Assistant or self-help diagnostics addresses connectivity and configuration problems, not stale cached profile data, and clearing a browser cache doesn't affect the desktop Teams client. **Learn more:** [User information isn't updated in Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/microsoftteams/teams-administration/user-information-not-updated)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes Teams. All users are assigned the Teams Premium add-on license.  
  
You have a team named Team1 that contains a channel named Quality.  
  
You plan to monitor audio and video quality during meetings for a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that the Quality channel receives a post whenever User1 experiences inbound packet loss that is greater than 5 percent during meetings.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Install the Microsoft Power BI connector for Call Quality Dashboard (CQD).

questions.explanation:
Teams Premium's alert rules, configured under Notifications & alerts > Rules in the Teams admin center, let admins monitor per-user call-quality metrics such as inbound packet loss, jitter, and round-trip time, and post a notification to a chosen Teams channel whenever a configured threshold is crossed. CQD/Power BI reporting is after-the-fact analytics rather than real-time channel alerting, and calling/template policies don't generate quality-based notifications.

**Learn more:** [Alerts for in-progress meeting audio quality issues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/alerts/alerts-in-progress-meeting-audio)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Office 365 subscription.  
  
You need to prevent guest users from deleting channels from a Microsoft Teams team.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: the Azure Active Directory Module for Windows PowerShell

questions.explanation: The Microsoft Teams PowerShell module provides the cmdlet Set-Team to configure guest settings including DeleteChannelsAllowed. This module is the programmatic tool for granular Teams configuration that GUI options in the admin center may not expose, enabling precise control over guest permissions.

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft Office 365 subscription. Within it, there is a Microsoft Teams group called Group1.  
  
You need to remove inactive users from Group1, and the membership of Group1 must be validated on a monthly basis.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: Data subject requests in the Microsoft 365 Compliance admin center
access reviews in the Azure Active Directory admin center
eDiscovery cases in the Microsoft 365 Compliance admin center
usage reports in the Microsoft Teams admin center

questions.explanation:
Access reviews (found in Microsoft Entra ID / Azure Active Directory admin center under Identity Governance) let administrators set up recurring reviews of group or application access. For a Microsoft 365/Teams group, you can configure a review to run on a defined schedule (e.g., monthly), have reviewers confirm each member's continued need for access, and automatically remove members who are denied or who don't respond, effectively removing inactive users. Data subject requests and eDiscovery cases are compliance tools for handling data privacy and legal investigations, not membership governance. Usage reports in the Teams admin center only show activity metrics and provide no mechanism to review or remove members.

**Learn more:** [Create an access review of groups and applications in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/create-access-review)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  

You have a team named R&D_Projects.  

You need to prevent guest users from being invited to R&D_Projects. The guest users must be able to be invited to other teams.  

What are two ways to block guest access to the R&D_Projects team? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Apply a sensitivity label to the R&D_Projects team.
From Azure PowerShell, run the New-AzureADObjectSetting cmdlet.
Configure a Microsoft 365 group expiration policy.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, disable guest access.
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, disable guest access.

questions.explanation: Two methods achieve per-team guest access control without affecting other teams: (1) Applying a sensitivity label with restricted guest access settings to the R&D_Projects team, and (2) Using the New-AzureADObjectSetting PowerShell cmdlet to configure guest access restrictions for that specific Azure AD group. Both approaches allow granular control at the team level rather than organization-wide.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company is upgrading from Microsoft Skype for Business Online to Microsoft Teams.  

The company's Microsoft Teams upgrade policy is set to Islands coexistence mode. The company plans to maintain the coexistence mode for several months.  

Several users report that they receive email messages about missed chat conversations.  

You need to recommend a solution to ensure that all the users receive chat messages.  

Which two actions should you recommend? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Install the Microsoft Teams clients on all the computers that run the Skype for Business client. Instruct the users to sign in to both client applications.
Instruct the users to modify the permissions in the Microsoft Teams client.
Modify the global app setup policy.
Modify the global app permission policy.
Install the Skype for Business client on all the computers that run the Microsoft Teams client. Instruct the users to sign in to both client applications.

questions.explanation: In Islands coexistence mode, each client (Skype for Business and Teams) operates independently. Both clients must be installed everywhere and users must sign into both to receive all messages from either system. App policies do not solve this; only client installation and dual sign-in enables message receipt across both platforms.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
Your company uses Teams.  
  
You plan to assign an enhanced encryption policy to enable end-to-end encryption for Teams calls.  
  
Which features support end-to-end encryption for one-to-one Teams calls?
questions.explanation:
When end-to-end encryption is enabled for one-to-one Teams calls, only the real-time media flow—audio and video—is end-to-end encrypted, while chat, file sharing, and presence continue to rely on standard Microsoft 365 service-level encryption rather than the call's E2EE. Options that include chat as end-to-end encrypted overstate what the enhanced encryption policy actually protects.\
**Learn more:** [End-to-end encryption for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-end-to-end-encryption)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E3 subscription that contains 500 users. All the users have computers that run Windows 10 and are joined to Azure AD.  
  
You need to generate a report that identifies which documents the users copied from Microsoft Teams to USB devices.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a custom data loss prevention (DLP) policy.
Assign the Enterprise Mobility + Security E5 add-on to each user.
Onboard the Windows 10 computers to Endpoint data loss prevention (Endpoint DLP).
Assign the Microsoft 365 E5 compliance add-on to each user.

questions.explanation: Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (Endpoint DLP) is required to monitor and report on files copied to USB devices. Endpoint DLP requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or E5 compliance add-on; the E3 subscription does not include this capability. Assigning the E5 compliance add-on is the first necessary step before configuring Endpoint DLP rules for removable storage monitoring.

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E3 subscription that contains 500 users. All the users have computers that run Windows 10 and are joined to Azure AD.  
  
You need to generate a report that identifies which documents the users copied from Microsoft Teams to USB devices.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a dynamic distribution group and configure a membership rule for the group.
Create an Azure Active Directory security group and add the Sales users to the group.
Create an Office 365 group and configure a membership rule for the group.
Create a new team by using the New-Team PowerShell cmdlet.

questions.explanation:
Teams are backed by Microsoft 365 (Office 365) groups, and dynamic membership rules based on user attributes (such as department) can only be configured on a Microsoft 365 group or a dynamic security group — not on a dynamic distribution group, which is an Exchange-only construct used solely for email distribution and cannot be converted into a team. The first step is therefore to create the Microsoft 365 group and configure its dynamic membership rule; the team itself is created from that group afterward.

**Learn more:** [Create a dynamic group](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-create-rule)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
You deploy a Teams Rooms device named Device1.  
  
You need to identify how many outbound meeting minutes were consumed during the last month by Device1.  
  
Which report should you run?
questions.explanation: The Audio Conferencing dial-out usage report tracks outbound dial-out minutes from meetings, including those initiated by Teams Rooms devices. This report shows per-device consumption metrics needed to calculate meeting minutes for devices like Device1.

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
You deploy a Teams Rooms device named Device1.  
  
You need to identify how many outbound meeting minutes were consumed during the last month by Device1.  
  
Which report should you run?

options.text: From Teams settings, modify the Email integration settings.
From Meeting settings, modify the Email invitation settings.
From Meeting policies, create a new meeting policy and assign the policy.
From Meeting policies, modify the Global (Org-wide default) policy.

questions.explanation:
In the Teams admin center, under Meetings > Meeting settings, there is an 'Email invitation' section where administrators can configure a Logo URL, Privacy and security URL, Help URL, and Footer text to brand meeting invitation emails sent to participants. This is the specific location Microsoft designates for customizing meeting invitation content, as opposed to meeting policies, which control meeting features and behavior rather than invitation branding.

**Learn more:** [Customize meeting invitations (IT admins) - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/customize-meeting-invitations)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
You are assigned the Groups Administrator role.  
  
You discover that you cannot create an expiration policy in Microsoft 365.  
  
You need to create the expiration policy. The solution must use the principle of least privilege.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Modify the global (Org-wide default) app permission policy.
Purchase a Microsoft Defender for Identity license.

questions.explanation: The Groups Administrator role is already the least-privileged, sufficient role for configuring Microsoft 365 group expiration policies at the tenant level, so a missing capability points to a license gate rather than a missing role: the feature requires an Azure AD Premium P1 (or higher) license to be present for group members. Requesting Global Administrator would violate least privilege since the role held is already adequate; the actual blocker to resolve first is the license.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Teams Phone deployment.  
  
You find that the Teams client can receive Teams calls but cannot receive PSTN calls.  
  
You need to ensure that the Teams client can receive both PSTN and Teams calls.  
  
What should you configure in the Teams client?
questions.explanation:
The **Redirect external phone calls** setting controls whether inbound calls from external callers, including PSTN callers, are sent to the user’s forwarding settings while internal Teams calls remain unaffected. Configuring this setting to avoid redirecting external calls lets the Teams client receive both PSTN and Teams calls.\
\
**Learn more:** [Teams Phone features - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/MicrosoftTeams/here-s-what-you-get-with-phone-system)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You plan to implement Microsoft Teams for 300 users.  

For the first stage of the deployment, you will enable the following features:  

✑ Audio  

✑ Video  

✑ Screen sharing  

Users will be prevented from using the following features:  

✑ File sharing  

✑ PSTN calling  

✑ Conference audio  

✑ Conference video  

✑ Conference screen sharing  

You need to calculate how much network bandwidth is required for the first-stage deployment.  

What should you use?
questions.explanation: Network Planner is the tool specifically designed to generate bandwidth requirement reports for Teams usage scenarios. It calculates network requirements based on usage patterns including audio, video, and screen sharing. For a 300-user deployment with defined feature enablement, Network Planner provides accurate bandwidth calculations for capacity planning.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  

You create a team named SalesProject.  

You need users to be added automatically to the team based on their department attribute.  

What should you do?

options.text: From the Azure Active Directory admin center, change the Membership type setting of SalesProject.
From the Azure Active Directory admin center, change the Group type setting of SalesProject.
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, modify the settings of SalesProject.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the settings of SalesProject.

questions.explanation: To enable automatic membership based on department attributes with least privilege, change the group membership type from 'Assigned' to 'Dynamic' in Azure Active Directory. Dynamic membership uses rules based on user attributes (like department) to automatically add and remove members, eliminating manual membership management.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  

You create a team named SalesProject.  

You need users to be added automatically to the team based on their department attribute.  

What should you do?

options.text: The user's Microsoft 365 license options in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center.
A meeting policy in Microsoft Teams.
A litigation hold on the user's mailbox.
A Sensitivity Label in the Security & Compliance Admin Center.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams private chat messages are stored in the hidden substrate folders of each participant's Exchange Online mailbox. Placing a litigation hold on a specific user's mailbox preserves that user's chat data from permanent (hard) deletion regardless of what the user does in the client, while affecting only that one user rather than every user in the organization. Meeting policies, license assignment, and sensitivity labels have no bearing on whether chat items can be purged.

**Learn more:** [Retention policies for Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/compliance/retention-policies-teams)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company is releasing a Request for Proposal (RFP) and is collaborating with four vendors. Each vendor must communicate with the company, but the vendors must NOT be able to communicate with each other in channel posts.  
  
The company must communicate internally about vendor specifics without the vendors having access to these communications.  
  
You need to create teams and channels in Microsoft Teams to support the communication requirements. The solution must minimize the number of teams.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create one team that has one private channel per vendor. Use the General channel for internal communications.
Create two teams per vendor. Use one team per vendor for internal communications.
Create one team per vendor. Use a private channel for internal communications.
Create one team that has two private channels per vendor. Use one of the private channels per vendor for internal communications.

questions.explanation: A team's standard (General) channel is visible to every team member, so putting all four vendors into one shared team would let them see each other's posts and violate the requirement that vendors not communicate with one another. Creating one team per vendor keeps each vendor's membership isolated from the others, and adding a private channel within each team lets company staff discuss vendor-specific matters without that vendor (who belongs to the team but not the private channel) having access, while still minimizing the number of teams needed for four separate vendor relationships.
