You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has recently purchased a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in your company have a  

Microsoft 365 E5 license.  

You have deployed Microsoft Teams to all users in the company. Several teams and channels have been configured.  

External contractors can access Microsoft Teams using guest accounts.  

You need to configure the environment to ensure that no files containing malware can be opened from Microsoft Teams channels by either company users or external contractors.  

Which of the following should you configure?
questions.explanation: Advanced Threat Protection (now Defender for Office 365) scans files uploaded to Teams channels for malware and blocks infected files from being opened by any user. This provides protection at the tenant level regardless of whether users are internal employees or external contractors.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
The organization is planning to host Microsoft Teams live events for audiences larger than 5,000 users.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that minimizes the bandwidth required to stream these events.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
When streaming Teams live events to very large audiences, Microsoft recommends using an eCDN (enterprise Content Delivery Network) solution. An eCDN provider caches and redistributes the live stream within the local corporate network (e.g., via peer-to-peer or local caching appliances), so that only a limited number of streams need to traverse the WAN/internet connection instead of every viewer pulling an individual stream. This significantly reduces the bandwidth demand on the network for large-scale events. SBCs and CVI relate to PSTN calling and third-party video conferencing interoperability, and third-party encoders are used to produce the live event content, not to reduce client-side streaming bandwidth.

**Learn more:** [Use eCDN solutions for Teams live events](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/ecdn-teams-live-events) · [Plan for Teams live events](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-live-events/plan-for-teams-live-events)

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a Microsoft Teams administrator for your organization.  
  
All teams used by the company's legal department must meet the following compliance requirements:  
  
- Each team must expire 365 days after it is created.  
- All team content must be deleted when the team expires.  
- An administrator must be able to restore deleted team content for 30 days.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the teams policy.
From PowerShell, run the New-AzureADMSGroupLifecyclePolicy cmdlet.
From the Microsoft 365 Compliance admin center, create a data loss prevention (DLP) policy.
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, modify the Office 365 group settings.

questions.explanation:
Because Teams are built on Microsoft 365 Groups, expiration behavior is controlled through a group lifecycle (expiration) policy, which is created or managed with the New-AzureADMSGroupLifecyclePolicy PowerShell cmdlet by setting GroupLifetimeInDays to 365 and applying it to Microsoft 365 groups. When a group/team is not renewed before its expiration date, it is automatically soft-deleted and its content removed, and Microsoft Entra ID retains soft-deleted groups for 30 days, during which an administrator can restore them. Neither the Teams admin center's teams policy, a DLP policy, nor the Office 365 group settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center provide this expiration/lifecycle configuration.

**Learn more:** [Set expiration for Microsoft 365 groups - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-lifecycle) · [Team expiration and renewal in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/team-expiration-renewal)

Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes the teams shown in the exhibit below.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783719576806-tszfsyvc.jpg)  
  
Guest users report that they are unable to create posts in the Monthly Reports channel.  
  
You need to make sure guest users can post to Monthly Reports.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams client, modify the privacy setting.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the Guest access settings.
From the Microsoft Teams client, modify the channel moderation preferences.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the messaging policy.

questions.explanation:
The Monthly Reports channel has moderation enabled, and its moderation configuration restricts who is allowed to start new posts — by default (or by prior configuration) this can be set to exclude guest users (e.g., the option "Everyone except guests can start a new post"). Channel moderation settings, including who can post and who the moderators are, are configured per channel from within the Microsoft Teams client itself (Manage channel > Moderation), not through the Teams admin center. Guest access settings in the admin center only control whether guests can be added to teams/tenant-wide guest capabilities, and messaging policies control tenant-wide messaging features — neither of these controls per-channel posting permissions governed by moderation. To resolve the issue, a channel moderator/owner must change the moderation preferences for Monthly Reports so guest users are permitted to start new posts.

**Learn more:** [Change moderator roles and settings in a channel in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/change-moderator-roles-and-settings-in-a-channel-in-microsoft-teams-6ac54758-3440-4f6a-9bd5-cebf97cb7ea6)

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783720763860-7xprdy3f.png)  
  
You create a new team named Project1.  

Which groups can be added to Project1?
questions.explanation: Only Group3 can be added to Project1. The maximum size of a distribution list or security group that can be imported into a team is 3,500 members. Group1 (11,500 members) and Group2 (4,500 members) both exceed this limit. Group3 (2,500 members) is within the limit and can be added to the team.

You need to integrate Microsoft 365 Defender with Teams to prevent users from uploading malicious files to a Teams channel.  
  
What should you do first?

From Safe Attachments, edit the Global settings.
Turn on the Built-in protection (Microsoft) Safe Links policy.

questions.explanation: To integrate Microsoft 365 Defender Safe Attachments with Teams for file protection, first enable protection in Safe Attachments Global settings by turning on 'Defender for Office 365 for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft Teams'. This global configuration must be enabled before creating individual policies.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Teams.  
  
You need to integrate Microsoft 365 Defender with Teams to prevent users from uploading malicious files to a Teams channel.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams client, modify the settings of the Sales team.
From the Azure Active Directory admin center, modify the membership type of the Sales group.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the properties of the Sales team.
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, modify the settings of the Sales group.

questions.explanation:
Because a Microsoft Teams team is backed by a Microsoft 365 group, automatic membership updates require converting the group to use dynamic membership. This is configured in the Azure Active Directory admin center by changing the group's membership type from Assigned to Dynamic User and specifying a rule (for example, based on the department attribute equal to Sales). Azure AD Premium P1 licensing, which the organization already has, is required to use dynamic group membership. None of the Teams client, Teams admin center, or Microsoft 365 admin center settings provide a way to automatically add users to a group/team based on attributes like department.

**Learn more:** [Create a dynamic group and check status - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-create-rule) · [Manage dynamic rules for groups in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-dynamic-membership)

questions.question:
You have a Teams deployment.  
  
You block access to several Teams apps.  
  
You need to ensure that users are redirected to a custom website to request access to the blocked apps.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation: The Org-wide app settings in Manage Apps provides the user request configuration feature, which allows administrators to redirect users to a custom website when they request access to blocked apps. This is where you configure the URL and custom message for blocked app requests.

questions.question:
You have a Teams deployment.  
  
You have a conference room that contains a Teams Rooms for Windows device named Device1.  
  
You need to customize the default meeting layout configuration for Device1.  
  
Which file should you modify?
questions.explanation: The SkypeSettings.xml file is the configuration file used for Teams Rooms for Windows devices. This XML file controls meeting layout settings and other device configurations and can be deployed remotely to customize the default meeting experience.

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
You have a Teams deployment.  
  
You have a conference room that contains a Teams Rooms for Windows device named Device1.  
  
You need to customize the default meeting layout configuration for Device1.  
  
Which file should you modify?
questions.explanation:
Meeting invitation branding elements such as the Logo URL, Legal URL, and Help URL are configured tenant-wide under Meetings > Meeting settings in the Teams admin center, so satisfying a requirement to customize meeting invitations requires modifying the Meeting settings.

Restricting a feature such as cloud recording to only a specific subset of users (e.g., a particular department) cannot be done by editing the global/default meeting policy, because that would apply to all users. Instead, an administrator must create a custom meeting policy with the desired restriction (such as disabling cloud recording) and assign that policy only to the targeted users or group, while the rest of the organization continues to use the global policy. This satisfies the requirement that only a specific group of users have the restricted behavior.

'Create a team's policy' is not a valid policy type for these requirements, 'Create a live events policy' governs live events/town halls rather than standard meetings or invitation branding, and 'Modify the Teams settings' controls unrelated app-level settings, not meeting invitation branding or per-user recording restrictions.

**Learn more:** [Manage meeting and events policies in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/meeting-policies-overview) · [Customize meeting invitations (IT admins) - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/customize-meeting-invitations)

All users are assigned a Microsoft 365 F1 license.  
  
You need to retain chats and files in Teams channels for at least one year after they are deleted.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Assign the users a Microsoft 365 E3 license.
Assign the users a Microsoft 365 F3 license.
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, enable Customer Lockbox.
From the Audit settings of the Microsoft Purview compliance portal, select Start recording user and admin activity.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft's Teams retention-policy guidance states that users subject to a Teams retention policy must have an appropriate license such as Office 365/Microsoft 365 E3 or A3; an F1 assignment alone is not called out as sufficient for enforcing chat and channel retention. Neither Customer Lockbox (governs Microsoft support engineer access to content) nor turning on Purview audit recording (a separate logging feature) grants retention rights, so licensing has to be fixed first.

**Learn more:** [Manage retention policies for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/retention-policies)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a Microsoft 365 subscription and uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
You need to ensure that only Microsoft apps can be used in Microsoft Teams.  
  
What should you do from the Microsoft Teams admin center?

options.text: From the global app setup policy, disable the Upload custom apps setting.
From the Org-wide app settings, disable the Allow interaction with custom apps setting.
From the Org-wide app settings, disable the Allow third party or custom apps setting.
From the global app permission policy, disable the Allow All Apps setting for Microsoft apps.

questions.explanation:
In the Teams admin center, Org-wide app settings (found under Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings) contains separate tenant-wide controls for Microsoft apps, third-party apps, and custom apps. Turning off the setting that governs third-party and custom app availability while leaving the Microsoft apps control enabled ensures that only apps published by Microsoft remain usable across the organization. This is the appropriate org-wide mechanism for restricting app usage by publisher category, as opposed to app setup policies (which control app pinning/upload for specific users) or app permission policies (which control per-user access to individual apps but do not provide an org-wide 'Microsoft apps only' toggle).

**Learn more:** [Manage your apps in the Microsoft Teams admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-apps) · [Manage custom app policies and settings - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-custom-app-policies-and-settings)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Teams.  
  
You have a room in Teams Rooms that contains a panel mounted at the entrance.  
  
You need to ensure that the panel displays a maximum room occupancy notification.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation: Maximum room occupancy notifications for Teams panels are configured through a configuration profile in the Teams admin center (Teams Devices > Panels > Configuration Profiles). This is not controlled by meeting policies, app setup policies, or notification rules.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has departments named Sales, Accounts, Research and Production.  

The company has recently purchased a subscription to Microsoft 365.  

All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E3 license.  

You are in the process of configuring Microsoft Teams. You plan to create a team for each of the company departments.  

All users have the Microsoft Teams desktop client installed.  

You need to ensure that the Research team is labelled as Confidential when viewed in the Microsoft Teams client.  

Which of the following actions should you perform?

options.text: Configure and publish a Sensitivity Label in the Security & Compliance admin center.
Configure and publish a Retention Label in the Security & Compliance admin center.
Configure a Teams policy in the Microsoft Teams admin center.
Configure the Meeting Settings in the Microsoft Teams admin center.

questions.explanation: Sensitivity Labels are configured in the Security & Compliance admin center and can be applied to Teams to label them with confidentiality levels such as Confidential. These labels automatically enforce end-to-end policies across the team. Retention Labels manage data lifecycle, not team classification; Teams and Meeting policies control different aspects of team functionality.

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription. You need to make sure that only members of the company's IT group are able to create private channels. Which three actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution. (Choose three; each correct selection is worth one point.)

options.text: Assign the members of the IT group to the policy.

questions.explanation:
Private channel creation permissions in Microsoft Teams are governed by the Teams channels policy (specifically the 'Create private channels' / AllowPrivateChannelCreation setting), not by the messaging policy. To limit private channel creation to a specific group of users, an administrator must disable the setting in the global (org-wide default) Teams channels policy so it is off for all users by default, then create a custom Teams channels policy with the setting enabled, and finally assign that custom policy to the members of the IT group. This combination ensures only users who have the custom policy applied—i.e., the IT group members—retain the ability to create private channels, while everyone else is restricted by the global policy default. The Set-TeamsChannel cmdlet manages properties of an existing channel and is unrelated to policy-based permission assignment.

**Learn more:** [Manage channel policies in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-policies) · [IT Admins - Private channels in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/private-channels)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Teams deployment.  
  
You have a Teams panel mounted at the entrance of a meeting space.  
  
You need to ensure that meeting attendees can extend or end a meeting space reservation from the panel.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation: Room-reservation behaviors on a Teams panel, such as allowing attendees to extend or end (check out of) a meeting space reservation, are controlled through the panel's configuration profile in the Teams admin center, under Teams devices > Panels > Configuration profiles > Meeting settings. A meeting policy governs meeting behavior for organizers and participants, an app setup policy pins apps, and a meeting template sets default meeting options, none of which expose panel reservation controls. **Learn more:** [Plan for Teams panels](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/devices/teams-panels)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Teams deployment.  
  
You need to customize the message that is displayed when a user requests access to a blocked app.  
  
What should you do in the Microsoft Teams admin center?

options.text: From Teams settings, configure the Notifications and feeds settings.
Configure the Customize app store settings.
From Manage apps, configure the Org-wide app settings.

questions.explanation: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, navigate to Manage apps > Org-wide app settings to find the user request configuration section. This is where you customize the message displayed when users request access to blocked applications.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Teams deployment.  
  
You need to customize the message that is displayed when a user requests access to a blocked app.  
  
What should you do in the Microsoft Teams admin center?

options.text: Attempt to locate a missing Teams meeting recording.
Validate that a specified user can disable Teams live events.
Validate that a specified user is configured to record meetings.
Validate end-to-end encryption for strictly confidential Teams meetings

questions.explanation:
The Teams self-help diagnostics catalog includes a "Missing Recording" diagnostic that tries to locate a meeting's cloud recording, and a "Meeting Recording" diagnostic that checks whether a specified user is correctly configured (licensed and policy-enabled) to record meetings. Guest-access review, disabling live events, and validating meeting encryption are not scenarios covered by this diagnostics catalog.

**Learn more:** [Self-help diagnostics for Teams administrators](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/microsoftteams/teams-administration/admin-self-help-diagnostics)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company uses Teams.  
  
You are assigned the Teams Communications Support Specialist role.  
  
You discover that you cannot read activity reports in the Microsoft 365 admin center.  
  
You need to be assigned a role that will enable you to read the activity reports. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should be assigned to you?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft documents that Microsoft 365 admin center activity/usage reports can be viewed by Global Administrator, Exchange/SharePoint Administrator, Reports Reader, Teams Administrator, and Teams Communications Administrator. The Teams Communications Support Engineer and Support Specialist roles are scoped to call-analytics troubleshooting and are not on that list, so moving up to Teams Communications Administrator is the least-privileged role that actually grants report access.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft 365 admin center activity reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/activity-reports/activity-reports)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  

You need to identify which teams were inactive during the past 90 days.  

What should you use?
questions.explanation: The Teams usage report (in the Microsoft 365 admin center or Teams admin center) lists every team together with a Last Activity Date column and lets you view activity over the last 7, 30, 90, or 180 days, making it the tool for spotting teams with no recent activity. The Teams user activity report is scoped to individual users rather than teams, and Teams advisor is a deployment-planning tool, not an activity reporting tool.

Your company has a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Phone System and Calling Plans.  
  
You plan to implement a toll phone number for the helpdesk.  
  
You need to implement the following call features for the helpdesk phone number:  
  
- Must include a greeting and hold music  
- Must bypass menu options when a call is established to the helpdesk  
  
What two resources should you create? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A call queue provides an incoming call greeting and music on hold while it searches for and connects the caller to an available agent, without presenting any dial-menu options—unlike an auto attendant, which is designed to offer menu choices to route calls. To assign the toll phone number directly to the call queue and receive external PSTN calls via Calling Plans, a resource account (licensed with Phone System and a Calling Plan, and assigned the phone number) must be created and associated with the call queue. This combination delivers the greeting/hold-music experience and lets callers reach the helpdesk without navigating any auto-attendant menu.

**Learn more:** [Setup - Call Queue - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/aa-cq-setup-call-queue) · [Manage - Resource accounts for Teams Phone Agent, Auto attendants and Call Queue - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/aa-cq-manage-resource-accounts)

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
You have a Teams Phone deployment that contains the components shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783713185268-wgbs1pz3.png)  
  
You need to enable automated callback for callers who are on hold for more than 10 minutes.  
  
What component should you modify?
questions.explanation: Automated callback for callers on hold longer than a specified duration is a feature of Call Queues in Microsoft Teams Phone. Auto attendants route calls, dial plans handle number translation, and routes manage traffic, but only Call Queues have hold management features.

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783713185268-wgbs1pz3.png)  
  
You need to enable automated callback for callers who are on hold for more than 10 minutes.  
  
What component should you modify?
questions.explanation:
The Call Quality Dashboard reports metrics like packet loss, jitter, and round-trip time, but it does not surface DSCP/QoS marking information, so it cannot confirm whether QoS tags are actually being applied on the wire. Microsoft Network Monitor lets you capture network traffic and inspect the DSCP value in the ToS field of packets, which is the only way to directly verify that QoS markings are present at the branch offices.

**Learn more:** [Implement Quality of Service (QoS) in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/qos-in-teams)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E5 license.  

All users use Microsoft Teams for collaboration. Several teams and channels have been configured.  

A team used by users in the Product Design department contains guest accounts. External Designers work with users in the Product Design department and access the team and channels using the guest accounts.  

The external designers report that they are unable to access files used in Microsoft Teams meetings or chats.  

You need to enable the external designers to access the files.  

Which of the following actions should you perform?

options.text: Modify the Guest access settings in Microsoft Teams.
Modify the External access settings in Microsoft Teams.
Modify the default Meeting policy in Microsoft Teams.
Configure the External Sharing settings in Microsoft SharePoint Online.

questions.explanation: Files in Teams are stored in the SharePoint Online site associated with the team. Guest access to these files is controlled by the External Sharing settings in SharePoint Online, not by Teams policies. Even if a guest has access to a Teams channel, they cannot access files unless SharePoint's external sharing policy permits guest access to the underlying site.

You are a Systems Administrator for your organization. Your company has recently purchased a subscription to Microsoft 365, and all users have been assigned a Microsoft 365 E3 license.  
  
You are planning to roll out Microsoft Teams to every user in the company. You need to make sure that only the company's managers are able to create new teams within Microsoft Teams.  
  
What should you do first to accomplish this?

options.text: Add all the managers to a Microsoft Team.
Add all the managers to a universal distribution group.
Add all the managers to an Office 365 group.
Add all the managers to a universal security group.

questions.explanation:
Controlling who can create Microsoft Teams (and the underlying Microsoft 365 Groups) is done by disabling group creation for everyone and then specifying an allowed group via the GroupCreationAllowedGroupId setting in the Azure AD directory settings (configured with the AzureAD/Microsoft Graph PowerShell modules). This setting must reference the object ID of a security group - not a distribution group and not a Microsoft 365 (Office 365) group - because only security groups can be used to scope this directory-level permission. Therefore, the first step is to create/populate a universal security group containing the managers, which can then be referenced when restricting group (and thus Teams) creation to that group's members.

**Learn more:** [Manage who can create Microsoft 365 Groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/microsoft-365/solutions/manage-creation-of-groups)

You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
The subscription is configured to display de-identified names in all reports.  
  
You need to publish reports on the usage of teams in the subscription. The solution must include only reports that support de-identified names.  
  
Which two reports can you use? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation: When de-identified names are enabled, the 'Teams user activity' report and 'Teams usage' report automatically de-identify user, group, and site names. These two reports support de-identification at the core level, making them compliant with privacy requirements. Other reports like 'Live event usage' and device usage have different privacy handling and should not be used in de-identified environments.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Case study -  
  
Overview -  
  
Company Information -  
  
ADatum Corporation is an energy company that has offices across North America and 3,000 employees.  
  
Physical Locations -  
  
ADatum has the offices shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783709320140-q1ydsl48.png)  
  
Existing Environment -  
  
Network Infrastructure -  
  
The office in Calgary has a 1-Gbps internet circuit. The offices in San Diego and New York have 100-Mbps internet circuits. The field site in Edmonton has a 3-Mbps internet circuit.  
  
Departments -  
  
ADatum has the following departments:  
  
• Information technology (IT)  

• Project management  

• Marketing  
  
Microsoft 365 and Tenants Environment  
  
ADatum recently purchased a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that has the Microsoft Teams Domestic Calling Plan add-on. All users are assigned Microsoft 365 E5 and Microsoft Teams Domestic Calling Plan licenses and Calling Plans is deployed.  
  
Azure AD has the default Cross-tenant access settings configured.  
  
The Teams policies settings are configured as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783709322620-7057n118.png)  
  
The Teams client is deployed to a non-persistent Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) used by the project management department.  
  
Allow guest access in Teams is set to Off.  
  
The Microsoft Viva Connections app is deployed to all users.  
  
Problem Statements -  
  
ADatum identifies the following issues:  
  
• An executive at the San Diego office reports that video drops during Teams meetings.  

• The Edmonton field site has limited bandwidth, and users report poor audio during Teams calls and meetings.  

• Users in the project management department report that they cannot give or take control during Teams calls and meetings while sharing their VDI desktop.  
  
Planned Changes -  
  
ADatum plans to implement the following changes:  
  
• Configure the media bit rate settings for the users at the Edmonton field site. The settings must apply only to the user while they are at the site, but NOT when they are at a different office.  

• Create a Teams channel to enable the project management department to collaborate with the IT department on a device upgrade project.  

• Implement a pilot rollout of Operator Connect for the users in the New York office. A port re-quest was accepted already.  

• Create a Teams channel for the marketing department for external collaboration.  

• Rename the Viva Connections icon as Start portal.  
  
Technical Requirements -  
  
ADatum identifies the following technical requirements:  
  
• The marketing department requires that all the files shared by using Teams remain available for at least three years after deletion.  

• The marketing department must be able to apply a watermark to content and video shared dur-ing Teams meetings.  

• All users require indefinite access to training videos recorded in Teams by the IT department.  

• All access to Teams and shared resources must use the principle of least privilege.  

• Guest access must remain disabled.  
  
Which license should you purchase to meet the technical requirements of the marketing department to apply a watermark?
questions.explanation: Watermarking for content and video in Teams meetings is a premium feature available exclusively with Microsoft Teams Premium license. This add-on provides enhanced meeting security and control features for organizations requiring advanced content protection and watermarking capabilities.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
You need to implement a solution to meet the Microsoft Teams requirements for the compliance department.  

What should you do first?

options.text: Add all the compliance department users as members of an org-wide team.
Add all the compliance department users to a security group.
Add all the compliance department users to an Office 365 group.
Assign the Teams Communications Support Engineer role to all the compliance department users.

questions.explanation: Restricting who can create Microsoft 365 Groups (and therefore Teams) is implemented by referencing a designated group's object ID in the group-creation policy, so the compliance users must first be collected into a group used for that policy. An Office 365 group is the type of object whose creation is being restricted, not the control mechanism, and there is no distinct role that grants group-creation exemption for this scenario.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft E5 subscription that uses Teams.  
  
You need to configure a policy to block specific words from being used as part of the name of new teams.  
  
Which type of policy should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Group naming policies in Microsoft Entra ID let administrators define a custom blocked-words list that is checked whenever a group or team name is created or renamed, preventing prohibited terms from appearing in Microsoft 365 Group and Teams names. Team templates, communication compliance, and terms of use policies address different concerns—team structure, content monitoring, and legal acknowledgment—and have no mechanism for blocking specific words in a name.\
\
**Learn more:** [Group naming policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-naming-policy)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that contains an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You plan to install the Teams for virtualized desktop infrastructure (VDI) client on Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts.  
  
You need to ensure that media optimization is configured for Teams.  
  
Which registry key should you configure on each session host?
questions.explanation: The registry key HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Teams with IsWVDEnvironment set to DWORD value 1 configures media optimization for Teams on Azure Virtual Desktop. This enables WebRTC redirection for improved call quality in virtualized environments.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: In the Azure Active Directory admin center, you change the **External collaboration settings**.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra External collaboration settings control B2B collaboration matters such as guest invitations, domain restrictions, and guest directory-access permissions, not Microsoft Teams meeting-camera capability. Teams controls guest video conferencing in the Teams admin center through guest-access and meeting audio/video settings.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure external collaboration settings for B2B in Microsoft Entra External ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-in/entra/external-id/external-collaboration-settings-configure) · [Turn guest access in Microsoft Teams on or off](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/set-up-guests)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: Place User1’s mailbox on Litigation Hold.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams private-chat messages are retained as compliance records in Exchange Online mailboxes. When a mailbox is on Litigation Hold, deleted or modified Teams-message copies in the SubstrateHolds folder are preserved and are not permanently deleted for the duration of the hold.\
\
**Learn more:** [Recoverable Items folder in Exchange Online](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/recoverable-items-folder/recoverable-items-folder) · [Learn about retention for Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/purview/retention-policies-teams)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the **External collaboration** settings.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Guest video use in Teams calls and meetings is controlled by the Teams **Guest access** configuration, where the **Video conferencing** capability can be turned off. External collaboration settings manage guest invitation and directory collaboration behavior, not the ability for guests to use cameras in Teams meetings.\
\
**Learn more:** [Turn guest access in Microsoft Teams on or off](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/set-up-guests) · [Secure external access to Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive with Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/architecture/9-secure-access-teams-sharepoint)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
Solution: You put the group mailboxes used by Microsoft Teams on Litigation Hold.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Teams private-chat data is stored in a hidden folder in the mailbox of each user participating in the chat, while Teams group mailboxes store channel-message data. A Litigation Hold on group mailboxes does not hold User1’s private-chat data, so it does not prevent that data from being permanently deleted.\
\
**Learn more:** [Learn about retention for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/purview/retention-policies-teams)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: You create an In-Place Hold for the Microsoft SharePoint site used by Microsoft Teams.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Private Microsoft Teams chat conversations are stored in the mailboxes of the participating users, whereas SharePoint sites store associated files and certain site-based content. A hold on the Teams SharePoint site therefore does not preserve User1's private chat messages; the relevant user mailbox must be placed on hold to retain private chats.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage hold policies for eDiscovery cases](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/edisc-hold-manage)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, modify the **Sharing** settings.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams camera and video access is controlled through Teams meeting policies, including the IP video and video-conferencing settings, rather than through Microsoft 365 Sharing settings. Therefore, changing Sharing settings does not prevent guest users from using cameras during Teams meetings.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage meeting policies for audio and video - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/meeting-policies-audio-and-video)

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the **External sharing** settings.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams External sharing settings control how users communicate or collaborate with people outside the organization, not whether guest users can use video cameras in meetings. Guest video capability must be governed through the applicable Teams guest-access configuration, so changing External sharing does not prevent guests from using cameras.\
\
**Learn more:** [Turn guest access in Microsoft Teams on or off](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/set-up-guests) · [Manage external meetings and chat with people and organizations using Microsoft identities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/trusted-organizations-external-meetings-chat)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: You create an In-Place Hold for User1’s Microsoft OneDrive for Business site.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams private chat conversations are stored in the mailboxes of the users who participate in them, while files shared in chat are stored in the sharer’s OneDrive. Preserving only User1’s OneDrive site does not preserve User1’s private chat messages; the user mailbox must also be on hold.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create holds in eDiscovery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/edisc-hold-create)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the **Guest access** settings.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Teams guest-access settings include a Video conferencing option. When this option is turned off, guest users cannot use video in Teams calls or meetings, preventing them from using cameras during meetings.\
\
**Learn more:** [Turn guest access in Microsoft Teams on or off](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/set-up-guests)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
Solution: Create a meeting policy and assign that policy to the users.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
A Teams meeting policy controls meeting features, not private user chat. Preventing private chat requires a Teams messaging policy with user chat disabled (`AllowUserChat` set to `False`), which prohibits private, group, and meeting chat for the assigned users.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy (MicrosoftTeams)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmessagingpolicy?view=teams-ps) · [Manage chat in Teams meetings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-meeting-chat)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
Solution: Create a messaging policy and assign that policy to the users.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
A Teams messaging policy can control chat availability for assigned users. Disabling the Chat setting (`AllowUserChat`) prevents users from participating in private, group, and meeting chats, so assigning such a policy to temporary employees prevents their use of private chat.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage messaging policies in Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/messaging-policies-in-teams) · [Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmessagingpolicy?view=teams-ps)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: You create a Teams policy and assign that policy to the users.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Private chat availability is controlled through a Teams messaging policy. Its Chat setting (the `AllowUserChat` parameter) enables or prohibits chat across private chats, group chats, and meetings; a Teams policy does not provide that control.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy (MicrosoftTeams)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmessagingpolicy?view=teams-ps) · [Manage messaging policies in Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/messaging-policies-in-teams)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
Solution: You create an app permission policy and assign it to the users.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Teams app permission policies control which Teams apps individual users can access. Private chat is a chat and channel messaging capability, which is controlled through Teams messaging policies; assigning an app permission policy therefore does not prevent temporary employees from using private chat.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage app permission policies in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-app-permission-policies) · [Manage Teams with policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-teams-with-policies)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the **External access** settings.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams external access settings apply to communicating with users in other organizations, whereas guest users are managed through Teams guest access settings. The guest access **Video conferencing** setting controls whether guests can use video in calls and meetings, so changing External access settings cannot prevent guest users from using cameras.\
\
**Learn more:** [Turn guest access in Microsoft Teams on or off](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/set-up-guests)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
You have a Teams deployment.  
  
You deploy the new Teams client to users.  
  
The users report that a third-party Teams store app fails to load.  
  
You need to identity the cause of the issue.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Enable Extended diagnostics data for the new Teams client.
Run the Microsoft 365 network connectivity test tool.
Run the Teams client in a browser and open the developer tools.

questions.explanation: Third-party Teams apps run as embedded web content, so the fastest way to identify why one fails to load is to reproduce the issue with the Teams web client and inspect the browser's developer tools (Console and Network tabs) for the failing request or script error. Enabling extended diagnostics data collects broader telemetry for Microsoft support but does not itself surface the specific load failure the way DevTools does.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You need to configure the user accounts of the sales department users to meet the security requirements.  

What should you do for each user?

options.text: From PowerShell, run the Grant-CsTeamsUpgradePolicy -PolicyName SfBOnly cmdlet.
From PowerShell, run the Grant-CsTeamsUpgradePolicy -PolicyName SfBWithTeamsCollabandMeetings cmdlet.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, set the Microsoft Teams upgrade policy to Skype for Business only coexistence mode.
From PowerShell, run the Grant-CsTeamsUpgradePolicy -PolicyName Islands cmdlet.

questions.explanation: Grant the Teams communication support engineer role to User1. This role provides permissions to view detailed call quality information, device information, IP addresses, caller/recipient names, and meeting participant details, while restricting access to administrative configuration. It follows the principle of least privilege by granting investigation access without full Teams admin permissions.

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
You need to configure the user accounts of the sales department users to meet the security requirements.  

What should you do for each user?

options.text: Configure a custom Configuration Profile that applies to the Marketing users.
Configure a custom Teams app Permission policy that applies to the Marketing users.
Configure a custom Teams upgrade policy that applies to the Marketing users.
Configure a custom Teams app Setup policy that applies to the Marketing users.

questions.explanation: App Setup Policies control which apps appear in the Teams client and their order. To add the Bookings app to the app bar for Marketing users, a custom app setup policy must be configured and assigned to that group. By default, all apps are permitted in the tenant. App Permission policies control which apps are allowed (not their placement), Configuration Profiles and Upgrade policies manage different settings.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a Microsoft 365 tenant that uses Skype for Business Online. All users connect to Skype for Business Online using computers running Windows 10.  
  
You are planning to upgrade all users from Skype for Business Online to Microsoft Teams.  
  
You need to ensure that the Microsoft Teams client is installed automatically on all the computers.  
  
What should you do from the Teams admin center?

options.text: From the Messaging policies settings, modify the Global (Org-wide default) messaging policy.
From Org-wide settings, configure the Teams upgrade settings.
From Teams apps, add an App setup policy.
From the Teams policies settings, modify the Global (Org-wide default) Teams policy.

questions.explanation:
The Teams upgrade settings, found under Org-wide settings in the Teams admin center, control how the tenant transitions from Skype for Business Online to Teams, including the coexistence mode and an option to automatically install the Teams client on users' devices as part of the upgrade process. Configuring these settings is what triggers automatic deployment of the Teams client to Windows 10 machines during the upgrade, whereas messaging policies, app setup policies, and Teams policies govern feature behavior within Teams rather than client installation.

**Learn more:** [Upgrade from Skype for Business to Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/upgrade-plan-decide-approach) · [Teams upgrade settings in the Teams admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/setting-up-your-tenant)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription. You need to stop users from using Microsoft Teams to communicate with users at a partner company whose email domain is litewareinc.com. What should you do from the Microsoft Teams admin center?
questions.explanation:
External access settings in the Teams admin center govern federation between your organization and other domains, allowing administrators to explicitly block or allow communication with specific external domains. To prevent Teams users from communicating with the partner company's users, the domain litewareinc.com should be added to the blocked domains list under External access. Guest access instead controls adding individual external users as guests within your tenant, messaging policies control chat/messaging capabilities for internal users, and meeting policies govern meeting behavior—none of these control domain-level external communication.

**Learn more:** [Manage external access in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-external-access)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Your company uses Teams.  
  
A user named User1 cannot invite guest users to Teams.  
  
What should you recommend using to identify the cause of the issue?
questions.explanation: Self-help diagnostics in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center is the appropriate tool to diagnose why a user cannot invite guest users to Teams. It identifies configuration and policy issues preventing guest invitations. The network connectivity test tool checks network health, Teams advisor provides guidance, and the network assessment tool is for network infrastructure evaluation—none are diagnostic tools for guest access issues.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E3 license.  

All users use Microsoft Skype for Business Online for collaboration.  

You plan to deploy Microsoft Teams phones to all users.  

A company policy has the following requirements for the Microsoft Teams phones:  

✑ The screen saver must be enabled and configured to start after 60 seconds.  

✑ Screen capture must be enabled.  

You need to configure the Microsoft Teams phones to meet the policy requirements.  

Which of the following actions should you perform?

options.text: Configure the Teams settings under Org-wide settings in Microsoft Teams admin center.
Configure a Teams App Setup policy in the Microsoft Teams admin center.
Deploy a configuration profile in the Microsoft Teams admin center.
Configure a Teams policy in the Microsoft Teams admin center.

questions.explanation: Configuration profiles in the Teams admin center (Teams Devices > Phones > Configuration Profiles) manage Teams phone device settings, including screen saver timeout duration and screen capture capabilities. This is the dedicated management tool for device-level configuration policies.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a Systems Administrator at a company that has a Microsoft 365 subscription, and all users hold a Microsoft 365 E3 license. All users rely on Microsoft Teams for collaboration.  
  
A company security policy states the following requirement:  
  
- All files used in personal chats or team collaborations must be retained for a minimum of one year.  
  
You need to configure a retention policy that satisfies this security requirement.  
  
Which two locations should the retention policy be applied to? (Choose two)
questions.explanation:
In Microsoft Teams, files exchanged in one-on-one or group (personal) chats are automatically stored in the participants' OneDrive for Business, whereas files shared in a team's channels are stored in the SharePoint site associated with that team. Because the requirement concerns retaining the files themselves (not just the chat/channel message text), the retention policy must include the OneDrive accounts location (to capture personal chat files) and the SharePoint sites location (to capture team collaboration files). The Teams chat and Teams channel messages locations control retention of the message content, not the underlying files, so they do not satisfy this specific requirement.

**Learn more:** [Learn about retention for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/compliance/retention-policies-teams) · [Where files are stored when you collaborate in Microsoft Teams](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/where-are-my-files-in-microsoft-teams-3f0899d1-3f16-4dcb-a1e2-3c1a4b64cf87)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has several departments.  

The company has a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E3 license.  

You have configured a Team for each of the departments. Each team includes several guest accounts for external contractors.  

A security policy has the following requirements:  

✑ Contractors must not be able to create channels in Microsoft Teams.  

✑ Contractors must not be able to update channels in Microsoft Teams.  

You need to implement the security policy.  

Which two of the following actions would meet the requirement? (Choose two)

options.text: Run the Get-AzureADGroup and Set-AzureADGroup PowerShell cmdlets.
Configure the Guest Access settings in the Microsoft Teams admin center.
Run the Get-Team and Set-Team PowerShell cmdlets.

questions.explanation: Guest channel restrictions require both Guest Access settings in the Teams admin center and the Set-Team PowerShell cmdlet (AllowGuestCreateUpdateChannels parameter). Option B configures the global guest permissions policy, while Option E applies it to specific teams. Both actions together enforce the requirement across all teams.

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E5 license.  

All users in the company use Microsoft Teams for collaboration.  

Users report that a team has been deleted in Microsoft Teams. The team was available yesterday.  

You need to restore the deleted team.  

Which tool should you use?

options.text: The Azure Active Directory admin center

questions.explanation:
A team is backed by a Microsoft 365 group, and within the 30-day soft-delete retention window the Microsoft Teams admin center's Manage teams > View deleted teams action lets an admin restore it directly. Because the deletion only needs to be reversed and no group-level Azure AD administration is otherwise implied, the Teams admin center is the most direct tool for the task (restoring the underlying Microsoft 365 group from the Azure Active Directory admin center within the same 30-day window is an equally valid alternative path).

**Learn more:** [Manage teams in the Microsoft Teams admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-teams-in-modern-portal)

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
You have a Teams deployment.  
  
You start a meeting and enable the following settings:  
  
• Enable Green room  

• Provide CART Captions  

• Enable end-to-end Encryption  

• Anonymous users can join the meeting  
  
What feature is no longer available during the meeting?
questions.explanation: When end-to-end encryption is enabled in Teams meetings, breakout rooms become unavailable. End-to-end encryption restricts several collaborative features including breakout rooms, together mode, large gallery view, and recording to maintain the encryption guarantee.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E3 license.  

You plan to host live events in Microsoft Teams.  

You discover that external users are unable to access the live events. Company users and users with guest accounts are able to access the live events.  

You need to configure the system to allow external users without guest accounts to access the live events.  

Which of the following should you configure?
questions.explanation: Who can join a scheduled live event is controlled by the "Who can join scheduled live events" setting inside a Live Events policy (Everyone, Everyone in the org, or Specific users/groups). Setting the default Live Events policy to Everyone lets fully external attendees join without needing a guest account, whereas the tenant-wide Live events settings only govern things like recording and third-party distribution, not attendee access.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment

options.text: Enable new external apps by default.
Allow external apps in Microsoft Teams.

questions.explanation:
Uploading a Teams app that has been packaged as a .zip file is known as sideloading a custom app. This capability is controlled in the Teams admin center under Teams apps > Setup policies, where the 'Upload custom apps' setting must be turned On for the relevant users. When enabled, assigned users can go to the Teams client, select Apps > Manage your apps > Upload an app > Upload a custom app, and select the .zip package provided by the developer. The other listed settings (allowing external/third-party store apps, or enabling new external apps by default) govern access to Teams Store apps and do not control the ability to sideload custom-developed app packages.

**Learn more:** [Manage custom app policies and settings - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-custom-app-policies-and-settings) · [Upload your custom app - Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/concepts/deploy-and-publish/apps-upload)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a user named User1.  
  
You need to assign User1 permissions to troubleshoot call analytics issues by using basic tools. Your solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation: The Teams Communications Support Specialist role grants permission to troubleshoot call quality and communications issues using only basic tools such as Call Analytics, which satisfies least privilege. The Teams Communications Support Engineer role includes access to advanced diagnostic tools such as Call Quality Dashboard, exceeding what is needed here. **Learn more:** [Use Microsoft Teams administrator roles to manage Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/using-admin-roles)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a user named User1.  
  
You need to assign User1 permissions to troubleshoot call analytics issues by using basic tools. Your solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?

options.text: From the SharePoint admin center, edit the External sharing settings for the associated site.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, configure the External collaboration settings for guest users.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, create a Conditional Access policy.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, set external access to Block all external domains.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, set Allow guest access in Teams to Off.

questions.explanation:
External sharing is scoped per SharePoint site, and Teams channel files live in the SharePoint site backing the team. Editing the external sharing setting for Team1's associated site blocks guest file access for just that team while leaving the tenant-wide Entra external collaboration settings, Conditional Access policies, and Teams external access/guest access switches (which apply org-wide) untouched.

**Learn more:** [Manage sharing settings for SharePoint sites](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/turn-external-sharing-on-or-off)

You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E3 license.  

All users use Microsoft Teams for collaboration.  

You need to prevent all users except managers from sending messages marked as Urgent.  

Managers must be able to send messages marked as Urgent.  

Which two of the following actions should you perform? (Choose two)

options.text: Configure a new Permission policy and apply it to the managers.
Configure a new Messaging policy and apply it to the managers.

questions.explanation: To implement the requirement, modify the default messaging policy to restrict urgent message capability for all users, then create a separate custom messaging policy for managers with urgent messaging enabled. This two-policy approach allows differentiated permissions while maintaining security for non-manager users.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that contains a Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops deployment.  
  
You plan to install the Teams for virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) client on virtual machines.  
  
You need to identify which Teams features are unavailable to the Citrix environment.  
  
Which two features should you identify? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation: In a Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops deployment of the Teams VDI client, screen sharing from chat and Give/Take control of shared content are the capabilities that remain gated: screen-sharing-from-chat requires a specific, later Citrix Workspace app build to function, and Give/Take control has repeatedly been called out in Microsoft's VDI documentation as not currently available in Citrix-optimized sessions. Multitenant Multi-Account, Channels 2.0, and sharing toolbar pinning/unpinning, by contrast, are already delivered as part of the Teams VDI client experience on Citrix. **Learn more:** [Microsoft Teams for Virtualized Desktop Infrastructure (VDI)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-client-vdi-requirements-deploy)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are planning a pilot project for Phone System involving 100 users. The pilot will use a Microsoft Calling Plan. You need to make sure the users can place calls to the PSTN. Which cmdlets should you run?
questions.explanation:
With a Microsoft Calling Plan, PSTN calling is enabled by: assigning the Phone System and Calling Plan licenses to the user (Set-AzureADUserLicense), enabling the user for Enterprise Voice (Set-CsUser -EnterpriseVoiceEnabled $true), and assigning a Microsoft-provided telephone number to the user (Set-CsOnlineVoiceUser -TelephoneNumber). Grant-CsOnlineVoiceRoutingPolicy applies only to Direct Routing deployments and is not needed for Calling Plan users, which is why the combination in this choice is correct.

**Learn more:** [MS-700 Exam Dumps – Phone System pilot Calling Plan cmdlets](https://www.freecram.net/question/Microsoft.MS-700.v2020-06-28.q35/you-plan-to-implement-a-pilot-project-on-phone-system-for-100-users-the-pilot-project-will-use-a-microsof) · [Set-CsOnlineVoiceUser](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/skype/set-csonlinevoiceuser)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Teams.  
  
You need to ensure that all the files in Teams channels are stored for at least one year after the files are deleted.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a retention policy for Microsoft SharePoint sites.
Create a data loss prevention (DLP) policy for Teams chat and channel messages.

questions.explanation: A retention policy for Microsoft SharePoint sites retains deleted files and content for a specified period. Since Teams channel files are stored in the underlying SharePoint document library, creating a SharePoint retention policy ensures files deleted from Teams channels are preserved in the recycle bin for at least one year, meeting the compliance requirement.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company uses Phone System.  

A group of users make outbound calls on behalf of the company's billing department.  

You need to ensure that when the users make the outbound calls, their numbers are replaced by a phone number that is associated to an existing call queue.  

What should you do first?

options.text: Create a new calling policy and set Make private calls to On.
Create a new calling policy and set Inbound calls can be routed to call groups to On.
Create a new caller ID policy and set Replace caller ID to Anonymous.
Create a new caller ID policy and set Replace caller ID to Service number.

questions.explanation: Caller ID policies control how the calling party's number appears to recipients. Setting 'Replace caller ID' to 'Service number' replaces the user's personal number with the associated service number (call queue number) on outbound calls. This ensures callers see the company service number instead of individual user numbers. Setting it to 'Anonymous' hides the number entirely, and Calling policies manage different call handling features.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription. An administrator reports that some teams were accidentally deleted today. You need to restore the teams as quickly as possible. Which cmdlets should you run?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams are backed by Microsoft 365 Groups, so deleting a team soft-deletes the underlying group, which remains recoverable for 30 days. The Get-AzureADMSDeletedGroup cmdlet lists the soft-deleted groups (returning their object IDs), and Restore-AzureADMSDeletedDirectoryObject restores a specific soft-deleted group by its ID, which restores the team along with its associated resources (mailbox, calendar, SharePoint site, and membership). Restore-ADObject applies to on-premises Active Directory objects, not Azure AD/Microsoft 365 groups, and Get-Team or Get-AzureADGroup do not return soft-deleted (removed) objects, so they cannot be used to identify what needs restoring.

**Learn more:** [Restore a deleted Microsoft 365 group or cloud security group - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-restore-deleted)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes Teams.  
  
You need to identify app data for a specific date and time range for the following:  
  
• Teams apps that were installed on or removed from a Teams client  

• Teams apps that were added to or removed from the Microsoft Teams app catalog  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From Compliance Manager, search the audit log.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, review Teams usage reports.
From Microsoft Teams apps in the Microsoft 365 admin center, review the App usage report.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, search the audit log.

questions.explanation: The Microsoft Purview Audit solution (accessed through Compliance Manager) provides comprehensive audit logs that capture app installation/removal events from Teams clients and app catalog changes within a specific date and time range. Other options provide only usage reports, not detailed installation events.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
You work as a Microsoft 365 Administrator for your company. All users have Microsoft 365 E5 licenses.  

All users use Microsoft Teams for collaboration.  

You upload a custom app to Microsoft Teams. The custom app will be used by all users in the company.  

You need to ensure that the custom app appears at the top of the app bar in Microsoft Teams.  

Which of the following actions should you perform?

options.text: Configure the global app setup policy.
Configure the global app permission policy.

questions.explanation: App Setup Policies are used to pin and organize apps in the Teams app bar. The global app setup policy allows administrators to add custom apps to the pinned app list and position them at the top (position 1). Configuration profiles are for device settings, Permission policies control which apps are allowed, and the general Teams policy does not manage app placement.

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783720963850-hwboaxni.jpg)  
  
Which groups can be converted into a team?
questions.explanation: Only Group2 can be converted to a team. Only Microsoft 365 groups can be converted to teams (not distribution lists or security groups). The maximum number of members in a Microsoft 365 group that can be converted to a team is 10,000. Group2 (Microsoft 365, 4,200 members) meets both criteria. Group3 exceeds the member limit at 15,200.

Town hall is the only Teams meeting template built for large one-to-many broadcasts: with Teams Premium it scales well beyond the 1,000-attendee webinar ceiling (extendable to 20,000 on request) and is the template that supports enterprise content delivery network (eCDN) integration for distributing the stream efficiently across a large audience. questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  

You need to generate a report that provides the following information:  

✑ How many users post and reply to channel messages  

✑ The number of ad hoc meetings organized by a user  

✑ The number of meetings a user has participated in  

✑ The total video time of a user  

Which report should you run?
questions.explanation: The Teams user activity report provides all required metrics: posts and replies to channel messages, ad hoc meetings organized by users, meetings participated in by users, and total video time per user. This report is specifically designed to show per-user activity across Teams collaboration and meeting features, making it the appropriate choice for this comprehensive activity reporting requirement.

questions.question:
You need to identify the requirements for the voice pilot project.  

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Assign an additional license and phone number to each user.
Deploy a Session Border Controller (SBC) for Litware.
Purchase a Phone System license for each user.
Create a dial plan for Litware.
Purchase a Calling Plan for Litware.

questions.explanation: Phone System deployment requires assigning an additional Phone System license to each user (A). Assigning phone numbers to each user (A) is mandatory. Purchasing Phone System licenses (C) is the prerequisite licensing step. SBC deployment, dial plans, and calling plans are secondary to the core requirement.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Teams.  
  
A group named Group1 collaborates with users from a partner company named fabrikam.com.  
  
You need to ensure that only the members of Group1 can create shared channels and invite users from fabrikam.com.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Configure an app setup policy in Teams.
From Inbound access settings, configure B2B direct connect for fabrikam.com.
From Outbound access settings, configure B2B direct connect for fabrikam.com.

questions.explanation: To let fabrikam.com users be invited into shared channels hosted in your tenant, you must add fabrikam.com as an organization and configure Inbound access settings for B2B direct connect so its users can be invited into your shared channels; to restrict which of your own users can create shared channels and invite those external users, you configure a Teams (channels) policy with shared-channel creation and external-invite options enabled and assign it only to Group1. Outbound access settings instead govern your users joining another organization's shared channels, and app setup or generic Teams settings don't control shared-channel creation rights. **Learn more:** [Collaborate with external participants in a shared channel (IT Admins)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/solutions/collaborate-teams-direct-connect)
