Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription. Using the Microsoft Teams client, you inspect the teams displayed in the exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783717207005-povzxu83.png)  
  
Members of the Retail team report that they are unable to create channels.  
  
You need to make sure the Retail team members can create channels.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
Note: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: From the Azure Active Directory admin center, change the membership type of the Office 365 group for the Retail team to Assigned.
From the Microsoft Teams client, promote all the Retail team members to an owner role.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, unarchive the Retail team.
Instruct the Retail team owner to restore the team by using the Microsoft Teams client.
From PowerShell, modify the information barrier policy.

questions.explanation:
The Retail team is archived, which places the team and its channels in a read-only state — members cannot create channels, post new messages, or make other changes until the team is unarchived. Unarchiving can be performed either by an administrator through the Microsoft Teams admin center or by the team owner directly from the Microsoft Teams client, both of which restore full functionality including the ability to create channels.

**Learn more:** [Archive or restore a team in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/archive-or-restore-a-team)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],What should you recommend to meet the Microsoft Teams requirements for guest access?

options.text: From the Azure Active Directory admin center, modify the External collaboration settings to include fabrikam.com only.
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, modify the Office 365 groups settings.
From the External access settings in the Microsoft Teams admin center, add fabrikam.com to the Allowed list of domains.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, turn off org-wide guest access and manually add guest users from fabrikam.com to teams.

questions.explanation:
Guest access to Teams and team resources is governed at the directory level by Azure Active Directory's External collaboration settings, which let you restrict invitations to specific partner domains such as fabrikam.com. Teams' External access (federation) setting only enables chat, calls, and meeting invitations between separate tenants' users — it does not grant guest membership in a team or access to its files and channels, so it does not satisfy a "collaborate in teams by using guest accounts" requirement.

**Learn more:** [Configure external collaboration settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/external-collaboration-settings-configure)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: You execute the `Grant-CsTeamsUpgradePolicy` cmdlet and specify the `-PolicyName` parameter.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
A Teams upgrade policy controls a user's coexistence mode and upgrade experience, not the version of the Teams client installed in VDI. Classic Teams installed by MSI with `ALLUSERS=1` has automatic updates disabled in VDI, so the client must be updated or redeployed to obtain new features.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Teams for Virtualized Desktop Infrastructure (VDI)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-client-vdi-requirements-deploy)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: Run the `Get-WUInstall` cmdlet and specify the `-AcceptAll` parameter.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Classic Teams MSI installations in VDI have automatic updates disabled. Installing Windows updates through `Get-WUInstall -AcceptAll` does not update the Teams client deployment, so it will not provide the new Teams features.\
\
**Learn more:** [Install Teams for Virtualized Desktop Infrastructure (VDI)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-client-vdi-requirements-deploy)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the Microsoft Teams upgrade policy.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Teams upgrade policy controls coexistence and upgrade behavior, not desktop-client version updates. A classic Teams MSI installation with `ALLUSERS=1` in VDI has automatic updates disabled, so gaining newly released client features requires updating or redeploying the Teams client rather than changing that policy.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Teams for Virtualized Desktop Infrastructure (VDI)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-client-vdi-requirements-deploy) · [Teams doesn't automatically update](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/microsoftteams/teams-sign-in/teams-doesnt-automatically-update)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question: Solution: Uninstall the Microsoft Teams MSI package, then reinstall a newer Microsoft Teams MSI package.
questions.explanation:
Classic Teams installed machine-wide through an MSI package in a VDI environment has automatic updates disabled. Updating the VDI image by uninstalling the existing package and installing a newer Teams MSI deploys the newer client version and its features to users.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Teams for Virtualized Desktop Infrastructure (VDI)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-client-vdi-requirements-deploy) · [Need to disable automatic updates for the Teams MSIX app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/1499510/need-to-disable-automatic-updates-for-the-teams-ms)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question: You need to resolve the notification issues that were identified during the pilot project. Which item should you modify?
questions.explanation:
The notification issue described in the pilot (users receiving repeated Teams notifications for about 20 minutes) is caused by the \"Send urgent messages using priority notifications\" option, which is configured in a Microsoft Teams messaging policy. Priority notifications alert the recipient every two minutes for up to 20 minutes or until the message is read. To resolve this, the global messaging policy applied to the pilot users must be updated to change or disable this setting.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage messaging policies in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/messaging-policies-in-teams)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Case study -  

This is a case study. Case studies are not timed separately. You can use as much exam time as you would like to complete each case. However, there may be additional case studies and sections on this exam. You must manage your time to ensure that you are able to complete all questions included on this exam in the time provided.  
  
To answer the questions included in a case study, you will need to reference information that is provided in the case study. Case studies might contain exhibits and other resources that provide more information about the scenario that is described in the case study. Each question is independent of the other questions in this case study.  
  
At the end of this case study, a review screen will appear. This screen allows you to review your answers and to make changes before you move to the next section of the exam. After you begin a new section, you cannot return to this section.  
  
To start the case study -  

To display the first question in this case study, click the Next button. Use the buttons in the left pane to explore the content of the case study before you answer the questions. Clicking these buttons displays information such as business requirements, existing environment, and problem statements. If the case study has an All Information tab, note that the information displayed is identical to the information displayed on the subsequent tabs. When you are ready to answer a question, click the Question button to return to the question.  
  
General Overview -  
  
Wingtip Toys is a manufacturing company that has 5,000 users, and locations across North America and Europe.  
  
Departments -  
  
The company has the following departments:  
  
• IT  

• Sales  

• Security  

• Customer support  

• Human resources (HR)  

• Research and development (R&D)  
  
Microsoft Office 365 Environment  
  
All users are assigned a Microsoft 365 E5 license and are enabled for Microsoft Teams Phone.  
  
Users in the R&D department are assigned a Teams Premium license.  
  
Requirements -  
  
Call Handling Requirements -  
  
Wingtip Toys identifies the following call handling requirements:  
  
• Inbound calls to the main telephone number of Wingtip Toys must be routed to the correct department by using an auto attendant.  

• During holiday periods, the auto attendant must perform the following actions:  

• Route customer support calls to the customer support department.  

• Play a recorded message for calls to all the other departments, and then disconnect the call.  
  
Meeting Requirements -  
  
Wingtip Toys identifies the following meeting requirements:  
  
• Meetings that include users from the R&D department must have a watermark applied to screen sharing sessions.  

• Once a quarter, the CEO of Wingtip Toys must host a live, online event that is attended by all users.  
  
Governance Requirements -  
  
Wingtip Toys identifies the following governance requirements:  
  
• New teams must meet the following requirements:  

• The Team type setting must be set to Private.  

• Users must be able to send emails to team channels.  

• Team members must be prevented from deleting messages from team channels.  

• Each team name must be validated against a list of blocked team names.  

• Each team name must contain a prefix of GRP and the department name as a suffix.  

• Team channels must include a pinned tab that displays the Wingtip Toys website.  

• When a user creates a team, the team picture must be the logo of the user's department.  

• The department manager of the user that creates the team must be assigned the Owner role for the team.  

• The use of animated GIFs must be prevented in team channels.  
  
Collaboration Requirements -  
  
Wingtip Toys identifies the following collaboration requirements:  
  
• Fabrikam users must be able to join team channels hosted by Wingtip Toys.  

• Wingtip Toys users must be prevented from joining team channels hosted by Fabrikam.  
  
Monitoring Requirements -  
  
A notification must be sent to users in the IT department when a Teams Rooms system goes offline.  
  
Pilot Project Requirements -  
  
Wingtip Toys is currently evaluating third-party call center apps that integrate with Teams. The security department mandates that all third-party apps be reviewed by a qualified analyst and comply with industry-standard frameworks.  
  
User Issues -  
  
Wingtip Toys users report audio and video issues when accessing Teams meetings by using a web browser.  
  
Business Requirements -  
  
Wingtip Toys identifies the following business requirements:  
  
• Follow the principle of least privilege.  

• Minimize administrative effort.  

• Minimize costs.  
  
What is the minimum compliance required for third-party apps to be included in the pilot project?
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 certification is the industry-standard compliance framework that provides comprehensive auditing, security controls, and compliance verification for third-party applications. This exceeds basic publisher attestation or verification and is what a security department would mandate for sensitive integrations like call center apps.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  

A user reports an error when he attempts to share his screen during meetings by using the Microsoft Teams Windows Desktop client.  

You need to collect the Microsoft Teams client log files from the user's device.  

What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams client settings, select Disable GPU hardware acceleration.
Select the Windows logo key + Alt + Shift +1.
From the Microsoft Teams client settings, select Enable logging for meeting diagnostics.

questions.explanation: Pressing Ctrl+Alt+Shift+1 in the Teams desktop client immediately generates and saves a bundle of Desktop, Media, and Debug log files to a local "MSTeams Diagnostics Log" folder that can be collected and sent for troubleshooting an existing screen-sharing problem. Disabling GPU acceleration is a workaround rather than a log-collection step, the Windows-key shortcut is not a valid Teams log shortcut, and enabling meeting-diagnostics logging only affects future meetings rather than collecting current logs.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment

options.text: Configure the Automatically admit users to Everyone setting in the global meeting policy.
Configure the Automatically admit users to Everyone in your organization setting in the global meeting policy.
Enable the Allow Meet now in channels setting in the global meeting policy.
Enable the Allow Meet now in private meetings setting in the global meeting policy.

questions.explanation:
The lobby bypass behavior in Teams meetings is controlled by the "Automatically admit people" setting in the meeting policy. To allow both internal and external (guest) participants to join a meeting directly without waiting in the lobby, this setting must be set to "Everyone." Setting it to "Everyone in your organization" would only bypass the lobby for internal tenant members, leaving external guests waiting for admission. The Meet now settings for channels or private meetings control who can initiate ad-hoc meetings and do not affect lobby/admission behavior.

**Learn more:** [Manage meeting policies in Microsoft Teams - Who can bypass the lobby](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/meeting-policies-participants-and-guests) · [Configure meeting settings in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/meeting-settings-in-teams)

Your company has a Microsoft Office 365 subscription.  
  
Users in the company’s sales department frequently invite guest users to meetings.  
  
You need to ensure that when the sales department users invite guest users to meetings, the guest users are admitted by default. The solution must only apply to the sales department users.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: In the global meeting policy, set Automatically admit users to Everyone.
Create a new meeting policy and set Automatically admit users to Everyone.
Apply the policy to the sales department users.
In the global meeting policy, set Automatically admit users to People in your organization.

questions.explanation: To apply guest auto-admit only to sales department users, first create a new meeting policy (not modify global) with 'Automatically admit users' set to 'Everyone', then apply that policy specifically to the sales department. This ensures the setting applies only to sales while other departments retain default behavior.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
Users report that when they attempt to add a third-party app named App1 to the Microsoft Teams client they receive the following message: "App1 needs permission to access resources in your organization that only an admin can grant. Please ask an admin to grant permission to this app before you can use it".  
  
You need to ensure that the users can add App1 without receiving the message.  
  
What should you do in the Microsoft Teams admin center?

options.text: Create a new app permission policy.
Modify the Org-wide permissions for App1.
Create a new app setup policy.

questions.explanation: When a third-party app requests organization resources, administrators must review and accept the app's permissions on behalf of the organization. This is done by modifying org-wide permissions for that specific app in the Manage Apps section of the Microsoft Teams admin center. Once approved, users can add the application without receiving permission prompts.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: Using PowerShell, you run the `New-AzureADPolicy` and `Set-AzureADPolicy` cmdlets.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
A B2B management policy can restrict which external domains may receive invitations, but the ability for guest users to send invitations is controlled separately through external collaboration guest-invitation settings. Both controls must be configured to allow only specified domains and prevent guests from inviting additional guests.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/what-is-b2b) · [Allow or block B2B collaboration with organizations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/allow-deny-list)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, you modify the global meeting policy.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
A global Teams meeting policy controls meeting-related behavior; it does not restrict which domains can receive guest invitations or prevent guest users from inviting additional guests. Domain restrictions and guest invitation permissions are governed by Microsoft Entra external collaboration and Microsoft 365 guest-sharing settings, which affect Teams guest collaboration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft 365 guest sharing settings reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/solutions/microsoft-365-guest-settings?view=o365-worldwide) · [Turn guest access in Microsoft Teams on or off](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/set-up-guests)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: Using PowerShell, you run the `New-CSExternalAccessPolicy` and `Set-CSExternalAccessPolicy` cmdlets.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Teams external-access policies govern federation with external organizations, not B2B guest invitation governance. Restricting invitations to specified domains and preventing guest users from inviting other guests require Microsoft Entra External collaboration settings, which provide collaboration domain allow lists and guest-invite permissions.\
\
**Learn more:** [New-CsExternalAccessPolicy (MicrosoftTeams)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/new-csexternalaccesspolicy?view=teams-ps) · [Configure external collaboration settings for B2B in Microsoft Entra External ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-in/entra/external-id/external-collaboration-settings-configure)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: In the Azure Active Directory admin center, modify the **External collaboration settings**.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra External collaboration settings can restrict B2B collaboration invitations to an allow list of specified domains. They can also limit who may invite guests; selecting a setting that excludes guest users prevents guests from inviting other guests.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure external collaboration settings for B2B in Microsoft Entra External ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/external-collaboration-settings-configure) · [Allow or block B2B collaboration with organizations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/allow-deny-list)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: In the Azure Active Directory admin center, modify the **External collaboration settings**.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?

options.text: Users receive chats and calls and schedule meetings in Skype for Business.
Users receive chats and calls and schedule meetings in Skype for Business but use Teams for group collaboration.
Users receive chats and calls in Skype for Business but use Teams for group collaboration and meeting scheduling.
Users use Teams as their only communication and collaboration tool.

questions.explanation:
In the 'Skype for Business with Teams Collaboration' coexistence mode, Skype for Business remains unchanged and continues to handle chat, calling, and meeting scheduling, while Teams is added only for collaboration capabilities such as teams/channels, file access, and apps. Teams private chat, calling, and meeting scheduling are disabled by default in this mode. This differs from the 'Skype for Business with Teams Collaboration and Meetings' (Meetings First) mode, in which meeting scheduling moves to Teams while chat and calling remain on Skype for Business. Since the scenario specifies the plain 'Skype for Business with Teams Collaboration' mode (not the 'and Meetings' variant), users continue to receive chats, calls, and schedule meetings in Skype for Business, and use Teams solely for group collaboration.

**Learn more:** [Understand Microsoft Teams and Skype for Business coexistence and interoperability - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-and-skypeforbusiness-coexistence-and-interoperability) · [Choose your upgrade journey from Skype for Business to Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/upgrade-and-coexistence-of-skypeforbusiness-and-teams)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Your company uses Teams.  
  
You plan to deploy Teams to a branch office that has limited bandwidth.  
  
Which two features can be used when the Teams client has a bandwidth restriction of 150 kilobit/s up and 150 kilobit/s down? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation: With 150 kilobit/s bandwidth restriction, only two features can operate: one-to-one video (requires 150/150 minimum) and audio during meetings (requires only 10/10). One-to-one screen sharing requires 200/200, screen sharing during meetings requires 250/250, and video during meetings requires 150/200, all exceeding the available bandwidth.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
Your company uses Teams.  
  
You plan to deploy Teams to a branch office that has limited bandwidth.  
  
Which two features can be used when the Teams client has a bandwidth restriction of 150 kilobit/s up and 150 kilobit/s down? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation: An auto attendant (E) provides the virtual receptionist functionality to route callers to either a specific user or a destination (the help desk). A call queue (B) handles the First-In-First-Out (FIFO) routing and queuing behavior for the help desk. These two resources together satisfy both requirements: the auto attendant as the entry point and the call queue for orderly help desk call distribution.

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E5 license.  

All users use Microsoft Teams for collaboration.  

A manager wants to be able to view the Microsoft Teams usage reports.  

You need to assign the manager permission to view the usage reports. The solution must use the principle of least privilege.  

Which of the following actions should you perform?

options.text: Assign the Teams Communications Administrator role to the manager.
Assign the Security Administrator role to the manager.
Assign the Reports Reader role to the manager.
Assign the Compliance Manager role to the manager.

questions.explanation: The Reports Reader role provides the principle of least privilege for viewing Teams usage reports in the Microsoft 365 admin center. This role grants read-only access to analytics and usage data without broader administrative permissions. Teams Communications Administrator, Security Administrator, and Compliance Manager roles grant significantly higher privileges than necessary for this task.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a Microsoft 365 subscription that contains several teams.  
  
The company’s security policy states that an administrator must be notified when a new team is created by using the Build a team from scratch option.  
  
You need to configure the environment to meet the security policy requirement.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Purview compliance portal, enable Communication compliance.
From the Microsoft Purview compliance portal, create an alert policy.
From the Azure Active Directory admin center, create a protection notification.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the global teams policy.

questions.explanation: Alert policies in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal are used to trigger notifications when specific events occur, such as team creation. This is the standard mechanism for alerting administrators about policy-relevant activities in Microsoft 365. Communication compliance and teams policies are used for different purposes.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: Assign the Teams Administrator role to User1.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Teams Administrator role grants administrative access to manage Teams devices, including remotely restarting them from the Teams admin center. Microsoft documents device restart as a Teams device-management capability and includes Teams Administrator among the roles permitted to manage Teams Rooms devices.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage devices in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/devices/device-management) · [Managing Microsoft Teams Rooms](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/rooms/rooms-manage)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: Assign the Teams Communications Support Engineer role to User1.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Teams Communications Support Engineer role provides access for call-quality troubleshooting and analytics, not device management. Remotely restarting Teams devices requires Teams device-management permissions, such as the Teams Device Administrator role.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use Microsoft Teams administrator roles to manage Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/using-admin-roles) · [Manage devices in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/devices/device-management)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: You give User1 the Teams Device Administrator role.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Teams Device Administrator role can manage Teams devices, including remotely restarting devices. Assigning that role to User1 grants the required permission.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage devices in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/devices/device-management) · [Use Microsoft Teams administrator roles to manage Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/using-admin-roles)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Solution: You assign User1 the Teams Communications Administrator role.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Restarting Teams devices remotely is a device-management action that requires the Teams Service Administrator or Teams Device Administrator role. The Teams Communications Administrator role does not provide the device-management permission needed to restart devices.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage devices in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/devices/device-management) · [Use Microsoft Teams administrator roles to manage Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/using-admin-roles)

Solution: You assign User1 the Teams Communications Administrator role.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?

options.text: From Guest access, set Allow guest access in Teams to On.
Edit the Meeting settings and set Anonymous users can join a meeting to On.
Edit the global meeting policy and set Private meeting scheduling to On.
Edit the live events policy and set Who can join scheduled live events to Everyone.

questions.explanation: External users invited via Outlook who are not part of the organization need to join as anonymous users. Enabling 'Anonymous users can join a meeting' in Teams Meeting settings allows them to join without a Teams or Microsoft account. Guest access and live events policies control different scenarios; private meeting scheduling does not affect external user join capability.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You need to configure the environment to meet the technical requirements for guest users.  

What should you modify from the Microsoft Teams admin center?
questions.explanation: Guest access settings under Users in the Microsoft Teams admin center configure the guest user policies for Teams. This is where guest permissions for chat, meeting participation, and feature access are defined. While meeting policies control specific meeting behaviors like lobby waiting, guest access settings provide the foundational guest user permissions configuration.

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
You need to configure the environment to meet the technical requirements for guest users.  

What should you modify from the Microsoft Teams admin center?
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Teams Call Quality Dashboard (CQD) provides detailed, aggregated analytics on call and meeting quality across the tenant, including specific network metrics such as packet loss, jitter, round-trip time, and bandwidth estimates. It allows administrators to break down quality data by location, subnet, or building, making it the appropriate tool for evaluating network-related call quality issues—like packet loss—when testing Teams calls to branch offices with limited connectivity. The Usage Report and Device Usage Report only provide adoption/usage statistics (e.g., active users, messages sent, device types) and do not report packet loss or call quality metrics, and there is no Microsoft tool called 'Network Testing Companion.'

**Learn more:** [Use the Call Quality Dashboard to assess Teams call and meeting quality](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/use-call-quality-dashboard-to-assess-quality)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has the offices shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783713193131-rq08lyrt.png)  
  
You have a Teams deployment.  
  
You need to apply bandwidth restrictions for Teams users in the Buffalo office. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
• The media bit rate must be 2 maximum of 1 Mbps.  

• Users that travel between the offices must have access to high-quality video while in the New York office.  
  
Which two features should you configure? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
A meeting policy sets the capped media bit rate of 1 Mbps for the Buffalo office, while a network roaming policy binds that restrictive policy to the Buffalo network site specifically; because a roaming policy only applies at the sites it's assigned to, users automatically get the uncapped meeting-policy settings once they roam to the New York site. Calling, Teams update policies, and Network Planner either govern unrelated settings or serve as a pre-deployment estimation tool rather than a live enforcement mechanism.

**Learn more:** [Network roaming policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/network-roaming-policy)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription linked to an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant. The tenant contains the groups shown in the table below.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783720136265-1d5lt2kz.png)  
  
You need to create a new team by using the Microsoft Teams client.  
  
Which group can you use to create the new team?
questions.explanation:
In Microsoft Teams, when you create a team from an existing group, only Microsoft 365 groups (formerly Office 365 groups) can be used, because a team is essentially a Microsoft 365 group with added Teams functionality (a shared mailbox, calendar, SharePoint site, and now a Team). Distribution groups, plain Security groups, and Mail-enabled security groups are not Microsoft 365 groups and do not appear as valid selections when creating a team from an existing group in the Teams client. Since Group3 is the only group of type 'Microsoft 365', it is the only one that can be used to create the new team.

**Learn more:** [Create a team from an existing team or group in Microsoft Teams](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/create-a-team-from-an-existing-team-or-group-in-microsoft-teams-f41a759b-3101-4af6-93bd-6aba0e5d7635)

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription and use Microsoft Teams.  
  
A user reports a negative Teams meeting experience.  
  
Your network team plans to troubleshoot the issue.  
  
You need to provide the network team with the IP address information used during the meeting.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Call Analytics in the Teams admin center provides per-call, per-user diagnostic details—including client, network, and device information such as IP addresses—for a specific meeting or call, making it the right tool to hand to a network team troubleshooting a poor meeting experience. Support and Recovery Assistant is meant for end-user self-service diagnosis, while client debug and media logs are raw local files that lack the structured network telemetry a network team needs.

**Learn more:** [Use Call Analytics to troubleshoot poor call quality](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/use-call-analytics-to-troubleshoot-poor-call-quality)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  

Users report poor call quality.  

You need to identify whether Teams calls use TCP or UDP.  

What should you review in the Microsoft Call Quality Dashboard?
questions.explanation: Quality of Experience Reports in the Microsoft Call Quality Dashboard display TCP and UDP protocol usage for Teams calls. These reports show which network protocol is being used for each call, allowing investigation of whether TCP or UDP is contributing to poor call quality issues.

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
Your company uses Teams Calling Plans.  
  
When a user places a Teams call to an ambulance service, you need to ensure that a notification is also sent to the main receptionist of the company.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation: An emergency calling policy (TeamsEmergencyCallingPolicy) is configured to specify who should be notified during emergency calls and how they are notified—via chat only, conferenced in and muted, or with unmute capability. This policy allows automatic notification of designated recipients (like a receptionist) when emergency calls are made, meeting the requirement to notify the main receptionist when a user calls an ambulance service.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Office 365 subscription that contains a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can view Usage reports in the Microsoft Teams admin center. The solution must use the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation: The Teams Administrator role is required to view Usage reports in the Teams admin center. While Teams Communications Support Specialist can view the Call Quality Dashboard, they cannot access the full Usage reports. Teams Device Administrator and Helpdesk Administrator do not have access to Teams admin center reporting capabilities. Teams Administrator provides the necessary least-privilege access for this requirement.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription and use Microsoft Teams.  
  
A user named User1 reports that the Redirect to a new number or contact option is unavailable in the Calls settings of the Teams client as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783713182181-lwghseve.png)  
  
What is the cause of the missing option?

options.text: Enterprise Voice is sabes for User1.
Busy on busy during calls is enabled for User1.
A policy that limits calls to domestic only is applied to User1.

questions.explanation: The 'Redirect to a new number or contact' option in Teams call settings only appears when Enterprise Voice is enabled on the user account. Without Enterprise Voice enabled, users can only redirect to voicemail or disable call redirection.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Teams.  
  
Users report that they receive a notification in their Teams client to fill in a survey and send the results to Microsoft.  
  
You need to use PowerShell to disable the notification.  
  
Which PowerShell cmdlet should you run?
questions.explanation: The in-product prompt asking users to complete a survey and send feedback to Microsoft is governed by Teams feedback policies, managed with the Feedback policy cmdlets; creating a custom policy with New-CsTeamsFeedbackPolicy (and setting the relevant survey/feedback parameters before granting it to users) disables the notification. Messaging, events, and app permission policies control unrelated chat, calendar-event, and app-permission behaviors. **Learn more:** [Manage feedback policies in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-feedback-policies-in-teams)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
Your company has 200 users.  

You plan to upgrade all the users from Microsoft Skype for Business Online to Microsoft Teams. Phone System with Teams must be enabled for all users.  

You need to recommend a coexistence mode for the Microsoft Teams upgrade policy.  

Which mode should you recommend?

options.text: Skype for Business with Teams collaboration
Skype for Business with Teams collaboration and meetings

questions.explanation: Phone System with Microsoft Teams is only supported when a user's coexistence mode is TeamsOnly; Islands, Skype for Business with Teams collaboration, and Skype for Business with Teams collaboration and meetings all keep Enterprise Voice/calling functions tied to the Skype for Business client or require voice on-prem. Since the requirement is for all 200 users to have Phone System enabled with Teams, the upgrade policy must move them to Teams only mode.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
Your company has 200 users.  

You plan to upgrade all the users from Microsoft Skype for Business Online to Microsoft Teams. Phone System with Teams must be enabled for all users.  

You need to recommend a coexistence mode for the Microsoft Teams upgrade policy.  

Which mode should you recommend?

options.text: Ensure that all users are signed in to either Microsoft Skype for Business or Microsoft Teams.
Change the coexistence mode to Teams only.
Ensure that all users have both Microsoft Skype for Business and Microsoft Teams installed and are signed in to both applications.
Change the coexistence mode to Skype for Business with Teams collaboration.

questions.explanation: In Islands coexistence mode, Skype for Business and Teams operate as fully independent, parallel clients that do not interoperate with each other's chat streams; a message sent from Teams is only visible to a recipient who is also signed into Teams (and likewise for Skype for Business). Until all 1,000 users have fully moved to Teams, the only way to guarantee nobody misses a message is to have every user keep both clients installed and signed in simultaneously.

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Teams Phone deployment that contains a resource account named Resource1 and an auto attendant named Attendant1.  
  
You plan to use Resource1 to provide call answering functionality for Attendant1.  
  
You need to ensure that Resource1 has a designated phone number.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From Active users in the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Resource1, and then select Devices.
From Resource accounts in the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Resource1, and then select Assign/unassign.
From Active users in the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Resource1, and then select Manage contact information.
From Resource accounts in the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Add.

questions.explanation:
Phone numbers for resource accounts (used by auto attendants and call queues) are assigned from Resource accounts in the Microsoft Teams admin center using Assign/unassign, not from Active users in the Microsoft 365 admin center, which has no option to assign a service number to a resource account.

**Learn more:** [Manage resource accounts in Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-resource-accounts)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E5 license.  

All users use Microsoft Teams for collaboration.  

An Office 365 group contains 300 users including 50 guest accounts. A Microsoft Team has been created from the group.  

You need to ensure that the group contains only members and guest accounts that require access to the group. Any members or guest accounts that are either inactive or no longer require access to the group should be removed. The solution must ensure that group membership is validated every month.  

Which of the following should you configure?
questions.explanation: Access Reviews are the designated solution for periodically validating group and team membership. They enable automated or manual reviews at set intervals (monthly in this case) to remove inactive or unnecessary members and guest accounts, ensuring the principle of least privilege. Conditional Access policies control authentication, Supervision policies monitor communications, and Teams policies manage team-level settings.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Office 365 subscription.  

You need to prevent guest users from deleting channels from a Microsoft Teams team.  

What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Whether guests can create, update, or delete channels in a specific team is controlled by that team's Guest permissions setting, found by going to the team's More options > Manage team > Settings > Guest permissions in the Microsoft Teams client itself — it is a per-team setting, not something configured tenant-wide from the Teams admin center, Azure portal, or Microsoft 365 security center.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set guest permissions for channels in Microsoft Teams](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/teams/teams-channels/set-guest-permissions-for-channels-in-microsoft-teams)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Teams deployment.  
  
From Microsoft Call Quality Dashboard, you discover that internal calls are marked as outside.  
  
You need to ensure that inside and outside calls are reported correctly.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation: When internal calls are marked as outside in Call Quality Dashboard, configuring Trusted IPs under Network topology tells Teams to recognize calls from those IP addresses as internal. This allows the system to classify calls correctly based on the calling location.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Teams and contains three teams named Team1, Team2, and Team3.  
  
You need to validate the owner of each team and identify the number of guest users that were added to each team.  
  
What should you use in the Microsoft Teams admin center?
questions.explanation: In the Teams admin center, the Manage teams page lists every team and, when you open a specific team, its Members tab shows the owners and each member's role, including a count of guest users added to that team. Usage reports surface adoption metrics rather than per-team ownership and guest detail, Teams advisor is a rollout-assessment tool, and Manage users is for individual user accounts, not team membership.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Teams and contains three teams named Team1, Team2, and Team3.  
  
You need to validate the owner of each team and identify the number of guest users that were added to each team.  
  
What should you use in the Microsoft Teams admin center?
questions.explanation:
Information barrier policies can be enabled on top of a Microsoft 365 E3 subscription by adding either the Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance add-on or the Microsoft 365 E5 Insider Risk Management add-on — either add-on independently unlocks the licensing requirement for information barriers, so each is a complete standalone solution. Microsoft Defender for Office 365 addresses threat protection, not information barrier policy licensing, and Communications Credits is unrelated to compliance features.

**Learn more:** [Learn about information barriers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/information-barriers-learn-about)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  

You need to ensure that only the following apps are available in the Microsoft Teams app store:  

✑ Lists  

✑ Project  

✑ Bulletins  

✑ OneNote  

✑ PowerApps  

The solution must minimize administrative effort.  

What should you do?

options.text: From the Manage apps page, block unapproved apps
Configure the global (Org-wide default) app permission policy
Configure the global (Org-wide default) app setup policy

questions.explanation: The global app permission policy allows you to set Microsoft apps to 'Allow specific apps and block all others,' then add only the approved apps (Lists, Project, Bulletins, OneNote, PowerApps) to the allow list. This configuration restricts the app store to display only these five apps while minimizing administrative effort through a single policy applied organization-wide.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription and use Microsoft Teams.  
  
You plan to support meetings that use breakout rooms.  
  
You need to recommend a breakout room solution that meets the following requirements:  
  
• Supports 500 participants  

• Supports content sharing and chat  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation: Breakout rooms are only available in standard Teams meetings, not in town halls, webinars, or live events. Since the requirement specifies support for 500 participants with breakout rooms and content sharing, a regular Teams meeting is the correct recommendation.

Your company has a Microsoft 365 subscription.  

You attempt to review call quality by location.  

When you sign in to the Microsoft Call Quality Dashboard, you discover that no locations are defined.  

You need to ensure that all the call quality information in the dashboard is segmented by location.  

What should you do first?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, configure reporting labels.
From the Microsoft Call Quality Dashboard, select Tenant Data Upload.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, run the Network Planner.

questions.explanation: The Call Quality Dashboard (CQD) requires tenant building data to be uploaded via the Tenant Data Upload feature to enable location-based segmentation of call quality data. This is distinct from Call Analytics, which uses reporting labels. The CQD Tenant Data Upload is the proper mechanism to associate network subnets and endpoints with physical locations so that call quality information is segmented by location.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E5 license.  

The company has several departments. You have configured a private team for each of the departments.  

You configure an additional private team named Managers. The Managers team will contain all departmental managers.  

You need to ensure that the Managers team is not viewable in the Suggested Teams list.  

What should you do?

options.text: Modify the member permissions for the Managers team.
Configure a new app permission policy.
Modify the Team discovery options for the Managers team.
Select the Hide option for the Managers team.

questions.explanation: Team discoverability (or discovery) settings control whether a team appears in the suggested teams list and directory. Modifying the team discovery options allows administrators to hide private teams from the suggested teams list while keeping the team functional for members who already know about it.

questions.question:
Your company uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
The company has 10 corporate images.  
  
You want to provide the images to users as custom backgrounds for Teams meetings.  
  
You need to make the backgrounds available to Teams users.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation: Custom meeting backgrounds in Microsoft Teams are configured through Meeting Policies in the Microsoft Teams admin center. Administrators upload corporate images and make them available to users through the Meetings > Customization Policies section. Meeting settings is a different location that does not contain this configuration.

questions.question:
Your company uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
You need to configure an auto attendant that will use a Direct Routing phone number to receive incoming calls.  
  
Which type of license do you require?

options.text: the Advanced Communications add-on for Teams

questions.explanation: Resource accounts used for auto attendants and call queues require a Phone System license, but because they are not interactive users they use the no-cost Microsoft 365 Phone System - Virtual User license rather than a paid per-user Phone System license. This requirement applies regardless of whether the resource account receives calls through Direct Routing, Calling Plans, or Operator Connect. **Learn more:** [Resource accounts for Teams Phone Agent, auto attendants, and call queues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/aa-cq-manage-resource-accounts)

questions.question:
Your company uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
You need to configure an auto attendant that will use a Direct Routing phone number to receive incoming calls.  
  
Which type of license do you require?

options.text: Start the information barrier policy application.

questions.explanation:
In Microsoft Purview Information Barriers, segments must be created before any information barrier policy can reference them, and policies must be created and applied only after the required segments exist. Therefore, the initial configuration step is to define the necessary information barrier segments (in this case, two segments to separate the R&D group from other users) before creating or applying any policy.

**Learn more:** [Learn about information barriers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/information-barriers-solution-overview) · [Define policies for information barriers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/information-barriers-policies)

questions.question:
Your company uses Teams.  
  
A user named User1 selects Forward my calls, and all incoming calls are forwarded to voicemail as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783708921206-9ft2qznc.png)  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can change the destination of the forwarded calls.  
  
What should you enable for User1?

options.text: Busy on busy when in a call

questions.explanation: Forwarding calls to a destination other than voicemail — such as a specific person, a call group, or delegates — requires the user's account to have Enterprise Voice (Teams Phone System) enabled. Without it, Forward my calls is effectively limited to voicemail as its only available destination, which is why User1's calls keep landing in voicemail regardless of the intended target; enabling Enterprise Voice unlocks the additional forwarding destinations.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Your company uses Teams.  
  
A user named User1 selects Forward my calls, and all incoming calls are forwarded to voicemail as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783708921206-9ft2qznc.png)  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can change the destination of the forwarded calls.  
  
What should you enable for User1?

options.text: Modify the department attribute of both users.
Invite both users to the HR team.
Add both users to the HR group.
Modify the privacy level of the HR team.

questions.explanation:
In this environment, Teams membership (including the HR team) is controlled entirely by dynamic group membership rules that evaluate the department attribute (for example, a rule equivalent to `user.department -eq "HR"`). Microsoft Entra ID automatically adds or removes users from a dynamic membership group whenever their attributes change, and members of such a group cannot be added or removed manually. Because the two pilot users are not appearing in the HR team, their department attribute value does not currently satisfy the dynamic rule. Correcting the department attribute on both user accounts causes Entra ID to re-evaluate the rule and automatically add them as members of the HR team.

**Learn more:** [Manage rules for dynamic membership groups in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-dynamic-membership)

You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You create an org-wide team named Team1. Users named User1 and User2 are the owners of Team1.  
  
You need to configure Team1 to meet the following requirements:  
  
- Ensure that only User1 and User2 can create new posts in the General channel.  
- Prevent @mentions for the org-wide team members.  
  
Which two actions should you perform from the Microsoft Teams client? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: From the Team1 settings, clear Give members the option to edit their messages.
From the General Channel settings of Team1, set the channel moderation preference to Anyone can post; show alert that postings will notify everyone (recommended for large teams).
From the General Channel settings of Team1, set the channel moderation preference to Only owners can post messages.
From the Team1 settings, disable all the Fun stuff settings.
From the Team1 settings, set Show members the option to @team or @[team name] to Off.

questions.explanation:
To restrict posting in the General channel to only the team owners, you must change the channel's moderation settings to 'Only owners can post messages,' which limits new posts to owners while still allowing replies (if permitted) from members. To stop members from being able to notify the entire org-wide team via @team or @[team name] mentions, you must disable the 'Show members the option to @team or @[team name]' setting in the team's member permissions configuration. These two settings together satisfy both requirements: channel moderation controls who can start new posts, while the @mention permission setting controls whether members can mention the whole team.

**Learn more:** [Set up and manage a moderated channel in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/set-up-a-moderated-channel) · [Manage member permissions and settings in Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-teams)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a team in Microsoft Teams named Team1 that has the channels shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783721286185-yy2l4866.png)  
  
Which channels support moderation?
questions.explanation:
Per the table, General and Channel1 are Standard channels and Channel2 is Private. Channel moderation is available only for standard channels that are not the General channel, and it is never available for private channels — Microsoft explicitly documents that moderation is unavailable for both the General channel and private channels even though General's underlying type is Standard. That leaves Channel1 as the only channel that supports moderation.

**Learn more:** [Change moderation settings for a channel](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/change-moderator-roles-and-settings-in-a-channel-in-microsoft-teams-6ac54758-3440-4f6a-9bd5-cebf97cb7ea6)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has a subscription to Microsoft 365 that includes Phone System. All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E3 license.  

You plan to configure an auto attendant. The auto attendant will have a nested auto attendant. The nested auto attendant will be used to provide a second-level menu that the first-level auto attendant can connect calls to depending on the option selected by the caller.  

You need to configure the auto attendants and required resources.  

Which of the following actions should you perform?

options.text: Create two auto attendants then create one resource account.
Create one resource account then create two auto attendants.
Create two auto attendants then create two resource accounts.
Create two resource accounts then create two auto attendants.

questions.explanation:
A resource account (with a Phone System license) is required only for an auto attendant or call queue that directly answers an incoming call. A nested auto attendant is reached by call transfer from the first-level auto attendant that already answered the call, so it does not need its own resource account. The correct order is to create the single resource account for the top-level auto attendant, then create both auto attendants (top-level and nested) and link them together.

**Learn more:** [Plan for auto attendants and call queues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/plan-auto-attendant-call-queue)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has implemented a Quality of Service (QoS) solution across its network. Microsoft Teams was recently rolled out to all users, each of whom works on a domain-joined computer running Windows 10.  
  
Users are reporting poor audio quality when using Microsoft Teams over the network. You have determined that the media traffic generated by Microsoft Teams is not being processed by the QoS solution.  
  
You need to make sure that all Microsoft Teams media traffic is processed by the QoS solution.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, set Insert Quality of Service (QoS) markers for real-time media traffic to On.
From the Microsoft Teams client, select a certified Microsoft Teams audio device.
From PowerShell, run the Set-CsQoEConfiguration cmdlet.
From Group Policy Management, create a Group Policy Object (GPO) that contains the Policy-based QoS settings, and then link the GPO to the domain.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, turn on logging for the device configuration profile.

questions.explanation:
Ensuring Teams media traffic is properly tagged and handled by a network QoS solution requires two coordinated configuration steps. First, in the Teams admin center, the setting to insert QoS markers for real-time media traffic must be turned on so that Teams applies DSCP values to audio, video, and screen-sharing packets. Second, because Windows requires Policy-based QoS port-range definitions before it will honor and preserve DSCP tagging for an application's traffic, a Group Policy Object containing the Policy-based QoS settings (with the appropriate UDP port ranges for Teams media) must be created and linked to the domain. Without this GPO, Windows will reset the DSCP markers Teams attempts to apply, so the network QoS solution never sees them. The Set-CsQoEConfiguration cmdlet relates to Call Quality Dashboard data collection, not to marking or preserving QoS tags, so it does not address the issue.

**Learn more:** [Implement Quality of Service (QoS) in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/qos-in-teams) · [Set-CsQoEConfiguration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/skype/set-csqoeconfiguration)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You plan to implement Teams.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to assess the current environment and identify configurations that must be updated to support Teams meetings and online conferences.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation: Advisor for Teams (Teams advisor) walks an admin through a Teams rollout by assessing the Microsoft 365 organization's current environment and identifying common configurations that must be updated or modified before workloads such as meetings and conferencing can be successfully deployed. Network planner instead focuses narrowly on bandwidth calculations, and the Office Deployment Tool and a generic "Microsoft 365 Assessment tool" are unrelated to assessing tenant configuration readiness for Teams. **Learn more:** [Use Advisor for Teams to help you roll out Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/use-advisor-teams-roll-out)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network includes an on-premises Active Directory domain that is synced to a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
Using the Microsoft Teams client, you create a new team named Sales.  
  
You need to make sure that the team automatically includes every user in the company's sales department, and that any new employees hired into the sales department are added to the team automatically as well.  
  
Which tool should you use to configure the membership of the Sales group?

options.text: the Azure Active Directory admin center

questions.explanation:
When a team is created in Teams, it is backed by a Microsoft 365 group. To automatically populate and keep that group's membership current with all sales department users (including future hires), the group's membership type must be set to "Dynamic User" with a rule based on an attribute such as department, and this dynamic membership rule is configured through the Azure Active Directory admin center (Groups blade), which requires an appropriate Azure AD Premium license. Active Directory Users and Computers only manages on-premises AD objects and has no concept of Microsoft 365 group dynamic membership. The Microsoft 365 admin center supports basic group creation/editing but not the dynamic membership rule builder. Azure AD Connect handles directory synchronization, not group membership rule configuration.

**Learn more:** [Create or update a dynamic group in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-create-rule) · [Manage Microsoft 365 Groups membership in Microsoft Entra](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/create-groups/manage-microsoft-365-groups-with-teams)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams and contains a distribution group named Group1 and a team named Project1.  

You add Group1 to Project1.  

100 new members are added to Group1.  

When will the membership of Project1 will be updated to reflect the changes to the group membership?

options.text: Only when the group is re-added manually to Project1

questions.explanation: Adding a distribution group to a team performs a one-time expansion: the group's current members are copied in as individual team members at that moment, and Teams does not keep a live link to the source group afterward. Subsequent additions to the distribution group are not propagated automatically, at any interval; the group must be re-added to the team to pick up the new members. The 24-hour sync behavior applies to changes made directly to team membership (e.g., via the admin center or PowerShell), not to group-based membership expansion.

questions.domain: Manage meetings and calling
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription. All users have computers running Windows 10 with Microsoft Teams installed.  
  
A user reports the following issues:  
  
- Users lose their connection during screen sharing.  
- The user selection process takes too long to complete.  
- The Microsoft Teams client crashes and restarts automatically.  
  
You need to view the Microsoft Teams debug logs to troubleshoot these issues.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams client, select F1. Open the ETL files in the %Appdata%\Microsoft\Teams\folder.
From the Microsoft Teams client, select Ctrl+Alt+Shift+1. Open the log files in the %Userprofile%\Downloads\ folder.
From Event Viewer, open the Application log and filter the log for a keyword of MSTeams.
Right-click the Microsoft Teams icon in the application tray, and then select Get logs. Open Logs.txt in the %Appdata%\Microsoft\Teams\ folder.

questions.explanation:
In the Microsoft Teams desktop client, pressing Ctrl+Alt+Shift+1 generates diagnostic/debug log files that capture detailed information about the client's activity, which can be used to troubleshoot problems such as dropped screen-sharing connections, slow performance during people search/selection, and unexpected crashes. These generated log files are saved automatically to the %Userprofile%\Downloads folder as text files. The F1 help shortcut and Event Viewer's Application log do not provide the same level of Teams-specific debug detail, and there is no built-in 'Get logs' context-menu option on the system tray icon that writes to a Logs.txt file in the Teams AppData folder.

**Learn more:** [Get Teams logs for troubleshooting - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/log-files)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Teams.  
  
Your company collaborates with a partner company named fabrikam.com.  
  
You plan to invite quest users from fabrikam.com to a standard Teams channel.  
  
You need to ensure that all the guest users accept your company’s terms of use (TOU) before gaining access to Teams.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure the Microsoft Entra Verified ID service.

questions.explanation: A Conditional Access policy with a Terms of Use condition enforces that guest users must accept the organization's terms of use before gaining access to Teams. Verified ID is for identity verification, access reviews are for periodic access confirmation, and PIM is for privileged identity management—none enforce ToU acceptance for initial guest access.

Your company collaborates with a partner company named fabrikam.com.  
  
You plan to invite quest users from fabrikam.com to a standard Teams channel.  
  
You need to ensure that all the guest users accept your company’s terms of use (TOU) before gaining access to Teams.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
The Quality of Experience report in Microsoft Teams' Call Quality Dashboard shows audio quality and reliability data for every client and device used in calls and meetings, including the capture and render devices such as headsets, speakers, and microphones. Filtering this report to User1 lets you see whether the audio streams from his headset were flagged as poor quality, confirming or ruling out the device as the source of the problem.

**Learn more:** [Use CQD to manage call and meeting quality in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/quality-of-experience-review-guide)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Office 365 subscription.  
  
You need to prevent guest users from deleting channels from a Microsoft Teams team.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: the Azure Active Directory admin center

questions.explanation:
From the team's profile page in the Microsoft Teams admin center, an admin can edit a team's Guest permissions, which include the option controlling whether guests can add or remove (delete) channels. This is the documented administrative control point for restricting guest channel-deletion rights across a team, independent of what any individual owner has set from the Teams client.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage teams in the Microsoft Teams admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-teams-in-modern-portal)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Office 365 subscription.  
  
You need to prevent guest users from deleting channels from a Microsoft Teams team.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
The default conferencing toll phone number is configured in the Audio Conferencing section found on a user's Account tab in the Microsoft Teams admin center. After navigating to Users > Manage users and selecting the user, an admin selects Edit next to Audio Conferencing under the Account tab and chooses a new number under Toll number. This setting determines the phone number shown in Teams meeting invitations sent by that user, and it is separate from Voice settings (phone number assignment/dial plans for calling), Calling policy (call handling features), and Meeting policy (meeting options), none of which control the audio conferencing toll number.

**Learn more:** [Manage the Audio Conferencing settings for a user in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-the-audio-conferencing-settings-for-a-user-in-teams)

Watermarking of shared content during meetings is a Teams Premium capability that is enabled and configured through a meeting policy, so assigning R&D users a meeting policy with watermarking turned on satisfies the requirement. Your company has a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You need to ensure that users from a partner company named Contoso, Ltd. can collaborate with your company's users in teams. The solution must ensure that the Contoso users can exchange chat messages in channels.  
  
Which three actions should you perform before you add the Contoso users to teams? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
*Note: Each correct selection is worth one point.*

options.text: From the Services & add-ins settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center, set Let group members outside the organization access group content to On.
From the Guest access settings in the Microsoft Teams admin center, set Allow guest access in Microsoft Teams to On.
From the External collaboration settings in the Azure Active Directory admin center, add Contoso's domain to the list of target domains.
From the External access settings in the Microsoft Teams admin center, add Contoso's domain to the Allowed list of domains.
From the External collaboration settings in the Azure Active Directory admin center, set Guest users permissions are limited to No.
From the Services & add-ins settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center, set Let group owners add people outside the organization to groups to On.

questions.explanation:
Enabling Contoso users to be added as members of a team (so they can participate in channel conversations) requires configuring Microsoft Entra B2B guest access rather than Teams external access/federation. This requires: allowing the Contoso domain in Microsoft Entra ID's External collaboration settings so guest invitations to that domain aren't blocked; turning on 'Allow guest access in Microsoft Teams' in the Teams admin center's Guest access settings, since guest access is an org-wide switch that must be enabled before any guest can be added to a team; and enabling 'Let group owners add people outside the organization to groups' in the Microsoft 365 admin center's Services & add-ins settings, because Teams membership is managed through the underlying Microsoft 365 Group and owners need this permission to add external guests to that group/team.

**Learn more:** [Guest access in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/guest-access) · [Collaborate with guests in a team (IT Admins) | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/solutions/collaborate-as-team?view=o365-worldwide)

Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes 200 Microsoft Teams users. Among these is a team called IT Support, which has 50 members.  
  
You need to make sure that outbound PSTN calls placed from IT Support display the company's IT helpdesk phone number as the caller ID. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
Which two tools should be part of your solution? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
(Choose two.)

options.text: the Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) PowerShell for Graph module
the Windows PowerShell module for Microsoft Skype for Business Online
the Skype for Business admin center

questions.explanation:
To display a specific number as the caller ID for outbound PSTN calls from a group of users, you create a Caller ID (Calling Line Identity) policy that substitutes the caller ID with a resource account's phone number, and then assign that policy to the entire IT Support group in a single operation rather than to each of the 50 members individually — this is what minimizes administrative effort. Creating/configuring the Caller ID policy and granting it to a group (via the GrantToGroup parameter set of Grant-CsCallingLineIdentity) are done with cmdlets from the Microsoft Teams PowerShell module. Since IT Support is a Team backed by a Microsoft 365 (Azure AD) group, the group's unique identifier (ObjectId) needed for the -Group parameter is retrieved using the Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) PowerShell for Graph module (e.g., Get-AzureADGroup). The Skype for Business Online PowerShell module and Skype for Business admin center do not manage Teams caller ID policies, and the Call Quality Dashboard is unrelated to caller ID configuration.

**Learn more:** [Grant-CsCallingLineIdentity (MicrosoftTeams)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/grant-cscallinglineidentity?view=teams-ps) · [New-CsCallingLineIdentity (MicrosoftTeams)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/new-cscallinglineidentity?view=teams-ps)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Microsoft 365 Administrator for your company. All users have Microsoft 365 E3 licenses.  

All users use Microsoft Teams for collaboration.  

A company security policy has the following requirements:  

✑ Meeting presenters must be unable to share their entire screen in meetings.  

✑ Meeting presenters must be able to share a single application window in meetings.  

You need to configure the system to meet the security requirements.  

Which of the following actions should you perform?

options.text: Modify the default Live Events policy.

questions.explanation: Screen sharing restrictions are configured in the Teams admin center via the default Meeting policy under Content Sharing settings. The 'Screen sharing mode' option can be set to 'Single App' to prevent presenters from sharing their entire screen while still allowing them to share a single application window. Live Events policies and general Meeting Settings do not provide this level of control.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams. All users are assigned Microsoft Office 365 Enterprise E3 license.  

You need to ensure that the users can join scheduled meetings by dialing a toll-free phone number.  

Which two add-on licenses should you assign to the users? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Audio Conferencing lets invitees dial in to a scheduled meeting from a phone, and toll-free dial-in numbers are billed per-minute against a Communications Credits pool rather than a Calling Plan, so both add-ons are required together to offer toll-free dial-in. Virtual User and Domestic Calling Plan licenses address resource accounts and outbound calling scenarios, not toll-free conferencing access.

**Learn more:** [Set up Communications Credits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/setting-up-communications-credits-for-your-organization)
