questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Office 365 subscription that contains a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can view Usage reports in the Microsoft Teams admin center. The solution must use the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation: Global Reader is the least-privileged role that provides read-only access to all Microsoft 365 admin centers, including Teams admin center usage reports. This role grants the minimum necessary permissions to view reports without administrative change capabilities, following the principle of least privilege.

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Teams.  
  
You have 200 Teams devices that are managed by using Microsoft Intune.  
  
You need to review real-time alerts when a Teams device goes offline.  
  
What should you use to configure the alert?
questions.explanation:
Real-time offline alerts for Intune-managed Teams devices are configured through a device state rule under Notifications & alerts > Rules in the Teams admin center, which monitors device health and near-real-time offline status and can post alerts to a channel or webhook. The usage report is historical, the Azure portal and Microsoft Endpoint Manager are not where Teams device health alerting is configured.\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Teams Devices Monitoring and Alerting](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/alerts/device-health-status)

questions.question:
Your company uses Teams.  
  
A user named User1 reports audio issues in meetings.  
  
You suspect that the issues were caused by an audio device or audio device driver.  
  
You need to identify which device and driver were used during past meetings.  
  
What should you do in the Microsoft Teams admin center?

options.text: From Usage reports, review the Teams user activity report.
From Manage users, review the Meetings & Calls tab.
From Manage users, review the Teams devices tab.
From Usage reports, review the Teams device usage report

questions.explanation: In the Teams admin center, navigate to Manage Users, select the user, go to the Meetings & Calls tab, select a past meeting by its ID, and then view the participant details to see which audio and video devices and drivers were used during that meeting. The Usage reports section only shows aggregate OS information, not specific device details.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Your company uses Teams.  
  
A user named User1 reports audio issues in meetings.  
  
You suspect that the issues were caused by an audio device or audio device driver.  
  
You need to identify which device and driver were used during past meetings.  
  
What should you do in the Microsoft Teams admin center?

options.text: Modify the global app setup policy.
Modify the global app permission policy.

questions.explanation:
An app setup policy lets administrators customize the apps that are pinned and visible by default in the Teams client's app bar (Activity, Shifts, Chat, Calling), while an app permission policy lets administrators control which apps (Microsoft, third-party, or custom) users are allowed to install or add in Teams. Because the requirement must apply only to the Sales group rather than the entire organization, new custom policies must be created (not the global/org-wide default policies, which apply to all users) and then assigned to the Sales group.

**Learn more:** [Manage app setup policies in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-app-setup-policies) · [Manage app permission policies in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-app-permission-policies)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft Office 365 subscription. Users in the sales department frequently invite guest users to meetings. You need to ensure that when sales department users invite guest users to meetings, those guest users are admitted by default. The solution must apply only to the sales department users.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
*Note: Each correct selection is worth one point.*

options.text: In the global meeting policy, set Automatically admit users to Everyone.
Create a new meeting policy and set Automatically admit users to Everyone.
Apply the policy to the sales department users.
In the global meeting policy, set Automatically admit users to Everyone in your organization.

questions.explanation:
Because the requirement must apply only to the sales department and not to the whole organization, you cannot modify the global (organization-wide) meeting policy, since that would affect every user. Instead, you must create a new custom Teams meeting policy and configure its 'Automatically admit people' setting to 'Everyone', which allows both internal and guest/external participants to bypass the lobby automatically. Setting it to 'Everyone in your organization' would only auto-admit internal users, leaving guests in the lobby, which does not meet the requirement. Once the custom policy is created with the correct setting, it must be assigned to the sales department users so that the behavior is scoped only to them, rather than applied globally.

**Learn more:** [Manage who can bypass the lobby in Teams meetings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/who-can-bypass-lobby-in-meetings) · [Manage meeting policies in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/meeting-policies-overview)

You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E5 license.  

You plan to deploy Microsoft Phone System.  

You need to configure the phone system with four unique greetings. The unique greetings will be used as follows:  

✑ One unique greeting will be used during office hours (Monday to Friday 09:00 to 17:00)  

✑ One unique greeting will be used outside office hours (Monday to Friday 17:00 to 09:00)  

✑ One unique greeting will be used during weekends.  

One unique greeting will be used during national holidays (for example, Easter and Christmas).  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783720449769-ftkvgmcw.png)  
  
You need to configure the system to meet the requirements.  

What is the minimum number of auto attendants you need to configure?
questions.explanation: A single Auto Attendant can be configured with call flow greetings for business hours, after-hours greetings, and holiday schedules that include separate greetings. While technically weekends cannot be configured as a separate time category independent of after-hours, they can be included in a dedicated holiday schedule with a unique greeting, allowing all four greeting requirements to be met with one Auto Attendant. Some implementations may use two Auto Attendants for cleaner architecture.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your Microsoft 365 subscription includes a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can view the Analytics & reports section in the Microsoft Teams admin center, while following the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation:
The Reports reader role is built specifically to provide read-only access to usage data and activity reports (including the Analytics & reports data shown in the Teams admin center) without granting any broader administrative permissions. This satisfies the least-privilege requirement, whereas Groups administrator and Skype for Business administrator provide unrelated administrative capabilities that exceed what's needed, and Global reader—while read-only—is a much broader role that grants visibility across nearly all Microsoft 365 admin workloads (more than is required) and does not reliably expose the Teams Analytics & reports data the way Reports reader does.

**Learn more:** [Reports Reader role description - Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#reports-reader) · [About administrator roles in the Microsoft 365 admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/add-users/about-admin-roles?view=o365-worldwide)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
You have a Teams channel named Project1.  
  
You have a third-party project management app named App1.  
  
You need to recommend an extensibility solution that integrates App1 into Teams. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
• Users must be able to access App1 directly from Project1.  

• The members of Project1 must be able to collaborate.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation: A tab is the extensibility solution that embeds web-based content directly into a Teams channel. Tabs allow users to access the third-party app from within the channel interface and enable team members to collaborate on the embedded content seamlessly.

questions.question:
You have a Teams channel named Project1.  
  
You have a third-party project management app named App1.  
  
You need to recommend an extensibility solution that integrates App1 into Teams. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
• Users must be able to access App1 directly from Project1.  

• The members of Project1 must be able to collaborate.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, set Download the Teams app in the background for Skype for Business users to On.
Create a Group Policy Object (GPO) that contains an app package, and then link the GPO.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, create an app setup policy that includes the Microsoft Teams app, and then assign the policy to all users.
From Microsoft Intune, push Microsoft Teams to all the devices.

questions.explanation: Intune is the multi-platform device management solution required for deploying Teams across Windows, Android, and iPhone devices simultaneously. The Teams admin center setting (A) only works for Windows PCs; GPO (B) and app setup policy (C) are Windows/desktop-specific.

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that has Teams Premium licenses, The subscription contains an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that has a session host named Host.  
  
You plan to install the Teams for virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) client on Host.  
  
You need to identify which Teams features will be unavailable to Host.  
  
Which two features should you identify? Each correct answer presents a complete solution  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation: Background blur and custom meeting backgrounds are not supported on Teams for VDI clients due to the processing overhead they require on virtual desktop infrastructure. End-to-end encryption, live captions, and multi-window functionality are available in VDI deployments. The visual processing demands of background effects make them unsuitable for virtualized environments.

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
Your company uses Microsoft Teams.  

A URL protection report shows many Blocked and clicked through actions.  

You need to prevent users from clicking through to blocked URLs.  

Which type of policy should you configure?
questions.explanation: Safe Links is a Microsoft Defender for Office 365 feature that provides time-of-click verification of URLs in Teams messages, emails, and other locations. It scans and blocks malicious links while preventing users from bypassing the warning to access blocked URLs. This is the appropriate security policy for controlling URL-based threats in Teams communications.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
Your company uses Teams.  
  
All users are assigned a Microsoft 365 E3 license.  
  
You need to recommend a license that will enable the use of information barriers (IBs) in Teams.  
  
What are two licenses that you can recommend? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: the Priva Privacy Risk Management add-on

questions.explanation: Information Barriers are available through two licensing options: Microsoft 365 E5 (includes all advanced compliance and security features) or the Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance add-on (provides compliance features including information barriers to E3 users). Either option provides complete information barrier functionality for Teams.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You need to configure the IP phones so that they satisfy the device requirements.  
  
What is the minimum number of configuration profiles you should create?
questions.explanation: Configuration profiles in Teams IP phones allow you to apply different sets of settings to different groups of devices. When requirements mandate distinct timeout or timezone configurations across subsets of phones, separate profiles are needed for each unique configuration. In this scenario, multiple policies are required to satisfy differing device requirements.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You need to configure the IP phones so that they satisfy the device requirements.  
  
What is the minimum number of configuration profiles you should create?
questions.explanation: Running teamsbootstrapper.exe with the -o option pointed at a locally stored or network-shared MSIX package lets every session host install the new Teams client from that local copy instead of each one downloading the package over the internet, minimizing bandwidth usage during a mass upgrade. PKG files apply to macOS, Microsoft 365 apps installation targets Office applications rather than Teams, and a plain standalone executable download would still pull the package from the internet per host.

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes Teams.  
  
When a user named User1 downloads and installs the new Teams desktop client on a Windows 10 device, the user receives the following error message:  
  
"We've run into an issue."  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can install the new Teams desktop client.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Clear the cache of the Teams desktop client.
Download and install the ASP.NET Core Runtime.
Start the Teams desktop client by using elevated permissions.
Download and install the WebView2 Runtime.

questions.explanation: The new Teams desktop client requires the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime, which ships built in on Windows 11 but is not guaranteed to be present on Windows 10; when it is missing or broken, installation fails with a generic "We've run into an issue" error, and installing or repairing the WebView2 Runtime resolves it. Clearing the client cache, running with elevated permissions, or installing the ASP.NET Core Runtime do not address this dependency and will not fix the install failure.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Teams deployment.  
  
You have a custom app named App1 that is uploaded to Teams.  
  
You need to ensure that App1 is pinned to the app bar for all users.  
  
What should you configure in the Microsoft Teams admin center?
questions.explanation: App setup policies in the Microsoft Teams admin center control which apps are pinned to the app bar for all users and their display order. This is the specific policy designed for managing app visibility and pinning across the organization.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
Users report poor call quality.  
  
You need to identify the source of the call quality issues and which locations are affected.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Run the Teams user activity report.
Upload building data to the Call quality dashboard.
Run the Teams device usage report.
Upload reporting labels for each location.

questions.explanation: The Call Quality Dashboard (CQD) is designed for analyzing call quality issues and network performance. After uploading building and network configuration data to CQD, administrators can generate quality-of-experience reports that identify poor call quality by location, building, and network segment. This is the essential first diagnostic step for triaging call quality complaints and pinpointing affected locations.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a Microsoft Office 365 subscription that contains default policies only.  

The company has the departments and teams shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783720118971-kgtz13qb.png)  
  
You need to recommend which policies must be created to meet the following requirements:  

✑ Users in the HR department must be prevented from sending messages marked as Urgent.  

✑ Users in the finance department must be able to send messages marked as Urgent.  

✑ Users in the finance department must be able to delete sent messages.  

The solution must only affect the HR department users and the finance department users.  

What is the minimum number of policies you should recommend creating?

options.text: one messaging policy and one permission policy

questions.explanation:
The default Global messaging policy already allows users to delete sent messages and send priority (Urgent) messages, so the Finance department's requirements are already met without any change. Only the HR department needs different behavior (blocking Urgent messages), which requires exactly one new custom messaging policy assigned to HR users — no permission policy is involved, since message deletion and priority notifications are messaging policy settings, not app permission settings.

**Learn more:** [Messaging policies in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/messaging-policies-in-teams)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a Systems Administrator for a company that has a Microsoft 365 subscription, and every user holds a Microsoft 365 E5 license. All users in the company collaborate using Microsoft Teams.  
  
A developer at the company is building a custom app intended for use in Microsoft Teams. Before releasing the app to all company users, the developer wants to test it in Teams. The developer has a .zip file that contains the app package for this custom app.  
  
You need to enable the developer to upload this app package to Microsoft Teams for testing purposes. The app must be available only to the developer within Microsoft Teams — not to any other users.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Modify the global app setup policy.
Configure an app setup policy that applies to the developer only.
Modify the global app permission policy.
Configure an app permission policy that applies to the developer only.

questions.explanation:
Uploading (sideloading) a custom app package into Teams is governed by the "Upload custom apps" setting within an app setup policy, not by an app permission policy (which instead controls which apps a user is allowed to install/interact with once they are available). To restrict this capability to just the developer, you must create/configure a dedicated app setup policy with custom app uploads enabled and assign that policy specifically to the developer's account, rather than editing the global (org-wide default) app setup policy, which would apply to every user in the tenant.

**Learn more:** [Manage agents and app setup policies in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-app-setup-policies) · [Manage custom app policies and settings - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-custom-app-policies-and-settings)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Active Directory user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can view the following reports:  
  
- Microsoft Teams user activity report  
- Microsoft Teams device usage report  
  
The solution must limit the ability of User1 to make changes to Microsoft 365 services.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation:
The Reports Reader role in Microsoft 365 provides read-only access to all usage reports in the Microsoft 365 admin center and Microsoft Graph reporting APIs, including the Teams user activity and device usage reports, without granting the ability to modify any Microsoft 365 service configuration. This satisfies both the requirement to view the specified reports and the requirement to restrict User1 from making changes to the tenant's services, unlike the Teams Service Administrator or Teams Communications Support Specialist roles, which include management or troubleshooting permissions beyond read-only reporting.

**Learn more:** [About admin roles - Microsoft 365 admin](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/add-users/about-admin-roles)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams and contains a Microsoft 365 group named Group1.  

The subscription has the Teams policy shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783720971425-yh4ilzn9.jpg)  
  
You need to ensure that the members of Group1 can create private channels. The solution must use the principle of least privilege.  

What should you do first?

options.text: Modify the Teams settings for the subscription.
Modify the Global (Org-wide default) policy and set Create private channels to On.
Create a Teams policy that has Create private channels set to On.

questions.explanation: Create a new Teams policy with 'Create private channels' set to On, then assign it to Group1. This follows the principle of least privilege by applying a specific policy only to the target group rather than modifying the global organizational policy. Direct policy assignment takes precedence over org-wide defaults, enabling precise control.

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has several departments including a Research and Development department.  

The company has a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E5 license.  

You have configured a Team for each of the departments.  

The Research & Development team has a channel named Design. The company plans to work with an external contractor to help design a new product. You have created a guest account for the contractor.  

The contractor reports that he is unable to post to the Design channel.  

You need to enable the contractor to post to the Design channel.  

Which of the following actions should you perform?

options.text: Configure the Global Meeting policy in the Microsoft Teams admin center.
Configure the external collaboration settings in Azure Active Directory.
Configure the Default Teams App Permission policy in the Microsoft Teams admin center.
Configure the Guest Access settings in the Microsoft Teams admin center.

questions.explanation: Guest access settings in the Teams admin center control whether guest users can post messages in channels. By enabling the appropriate messaging permission for guests in these settings, contractors can be granted the ability to post to specific channels like the Design channel.

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft Office 365 subscription.  
  
You discover that apps from a certain third-party publisher have security issues.  
  
You need to block all apps from that publisher.  
  
What should you use in the Microsoft Teams admin center?
questions.explanation:
In the Teams admin center, the Manage apps page (Teams apps > Manage apps) lists every available app along with details such as its publisher, and lets an admin select one or more apps and set their status to Allowed or Blocked. Because the requirement is to block every app originating from one specific third-party publisher — not all third-party apps in general — the admin must locate each app from that publisher in the Manage apps list (which can be sorted/filtered by publisher) and block them individually or as a multi-select action. Org-wide app settings only provides a single bulk switch for all third-party apps as a category and cannot isolate one particular publisher, and Policy packages and Permission policies govern which already-classified apps are exposed to specific user groups rather than performing the actual allow/block action on the apps themselves.

**Learn more:** [Manage your apps in the Microsoft Teams admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/manage-apps)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
You need to prevent users from creating private channels.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation: Teams policies control organization-wide channel creation settings. To prevent all users from creating private channels across the organization, create or modify a Teams policy and disable the 'Create private channels' option. Modifying individual team settings applies only to that team; policies apply organization-wide following least-privilege principles.

You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
You need to prevent users from creating private channels.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Provide the Emergency Location Identification Number (ELIN) associated with the emergency address.
Create an emergency call routing policy.
Specify the latitude and longitude of the location.

questions.explanation:
When Teams cannot automatically validate an emergency address against the mapping service, an administrator can manually complete validation by supplying the precise latitude and longitude of the location, either in the Teams admin center when adding the address or via the -Latitude and -Longitude parameters of Set-CsOnlineLisCivicAddress in PowerShell.

**Learn more:** [Manage emergency locations - Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/add-change-remove-emergency-location-organization)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work as a Systems Administrator for your company. The company has recently purchased a subscription to Microsoft 365. All users in your company have a Microsoft 365 E3 license. You are in the process of configuring Microsoft Teams.  
  
A company security policy states that users must not be able to add apps to Microsoft Teams.  
  
You need to configure Microsoft Teams to meet this security requirement.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
App permission policies in the Microsoft Teams admin center determine which apps (Microsoft, third-party, and custom) users are allowed to install and use in Teams. By editing the global (Org-wide default) app permission policy and setting Microsoft apps, third-party apps, and custom apps to blocked, an administrator prevents users from adding any apps to Teams. This differs from the Teams policy, which governs meeting/calling/messaging capabilities; Org-wide settings, which control features like email integration and cloud file storage; and the app setup policy, which manages pinned/preinstalled apps and custom app uploading rather than the fundamental permission to add apps.

**Learn more:** [Manage app permission policies in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-app-permission-policies)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes Microsoft Teams. You purchase an app called App1 from the Microsoft Teams Store. You need to make App1 available in the Microsoft Teams client, but only for a specific group of users.  
  
Which two actions should you perform from the Microsoft Teams admin center? (Each correct answer presents part of the solution. Each correct selection is worth one point.)

options.text: From the Meeting settings, modify the Network settings.
From App setup policies, create a new app setup policy.
From App setup policies, modify the global app setup policy.
From the properties of each user, edit the assigned policies.
From the Teams settings, modify the Devices settings.

questions.explanation:
App setup policies in the Teams admin center control which apps are pinned or installed by default for users. Since the app should be available only to a specific group rather than the whole tenant, you must create a new (custom) app setup policy—rather than modifying the global policy, which applies org-wide—and add App1 to it. You then target the specific users by assigning that custom policy to them, which can be done from each user's account properties (Assigned policies) in the Teams admin center. This combination scopes App1's availability to only the intended users, consistent with Microsoft's guidance on managing app setup policies (Teams apps > Setup policies) and assigning policies to users and groups.

**Learn more:** [Manage app setup policies in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-app-setup-policies) · [Assign policies to users and groups - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/assign-policies-users-and-groups)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to ensure that file sharing in Teams chats meets the marketing department’s technical requirements.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a retention policy for the SharePoint sites location.
Create a retention policy for Teams chats.
Create a data loss prevention (DLP) policy for Teams chat and channel messages.
Create a retention policy for the OneDrive accounts location.

questions.explanation:
Files shared in a Microsoft Teams chat are stored in the OneDrive account of the user who shared them. A retention policy for the **OneDrive accounts** location can retain those files for at least three years after deletion. SharePoint site retention applies to channel files, and Teams-chat retention applies to messages rather than the associated OneDrive files.

**Learn more:** [Create and configure retention policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/create-retention-policies) · [Learn about retention for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/retention-policies-teams)

questions.question:
You need to implement the planned change for the Edmonton field site.  
  
What should you create?
questions.explanation:
A Teams network roaming policy supports location-based media bitrate settings. Assigning it to the Edmonton network site causes its limits to apply only when a Teams client connects from that site; users receive their other applicable settings when they connect elsewhere.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage video and media settings with the network roaming policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/network-roaming-policy) · [New-CsTeamsNetworkRoamingPolicy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/new-csteamsnetworkroamingpolicy?view=teams-ps)

questions.question:
You need to address the issue reported by the project management department users.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Instruct the users to launch Teams and select Check for updates.
Uninstall the current Teams client, and then reinstall the latest version of the client.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, create and assign a new meeting policy.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the Meeting settings.

questions.explanation:
The ability to give, receive, or request control of a shared desktop or window is controlled by the per-user **Participants can give or request control** setting in a Teams meeting policy. Assigning a meeting policy with that setting enabled to the project management users allows the required sharing-control capability.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage who can present and request control in Teams meetings and events](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/MicrosoftTeams/meeting-who-present-request-control)

questions.domain: Configure and manage a Teams environment
questions.question:
You need to address the issue reported by the project management department users.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Set Invite external users to shared channels to On for the Global (Org-wide default) Teams policy.
From the Azure Active Directory admin center, configure the B2B direct connect outbound access settings for external users and groups.
From the Azure Active Directory admin center, configure the B2B direct connect inbound access settings for external users and groups.
Set Join external shared channels to On for the Teams policy of the marketing department.
Set Invite external users to shared channels to On for the Teams policy of the marketing department.

questions.explanation:
External collaboration in a Teams shared channel uses Microsoft Entra B2B direct connect, allowing external participants without adding them as Teams guests. The marketing custom Teams policy must allow its channel owners to invite external users to shared channels. The resource organization must also allow B2B direct connect inbound access for the external users and groups that will be invited to its shared channel. Outbound access and the ability to join external shared channels apply when the organization’s users are invited to a shared channel hosted elsewhere.

**Learn more:** [Collaborate with external participants in a shared channel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/microsoft-365/solutions/collaborate-teams-direct-connect) · [B2B direct connect overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/b2b-direct-connect-overview)

questions.domain: Monitor, report on, and troubleshoot Teams
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams, along with 300 Microsoft Teams-certified IP phones.  
  
You need a way to locate, group, and filter the IP phones based on keywords.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Device tags in the Microsoft Teams admin center let administrators assign one or more keyword-based tags to devices, including IP phones. Once tags are applied, admins can use the Filter option in the device pane to search for devices matching a specified tag (or combination of tags), effectively locating, grouping, and filtering devices based on those keywords. This also enables performing bulk actions—such as applying configuration policies or firmware updates—on the filtered set of devices. Reporting labels, by contrast, are used only to map physical office locations to network subnets for use in Call Analytics and Call Quality Dashboard reports, and do not support device grouping or filtering.

**Learn more:** [Manage and filter Microsoft Teams device tags](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/devices/manage-device-tags) · [Manage devices in Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/devices/device-management)

questions.domain: Manage teams, channels, chats, and apps
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes 200 Microsoft Teams users and 20 teams.  
  
You notice that several teams currently have no owner assigned.  
  
You need to make sure that you receive a notification whenever a team is missing an owner.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, modify the Teams settings.
From PowerShell, run the Set-Team cmdlet.
From the Azure Active Directory admin center, modify the group expiration settings.
From PowerShell, run the Add-AzureADMSLifecyclePolicyGroup cmdlet.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft 365 Groups (which underlie Teams) support an expiration/lifecycle policy in Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD). Part of configuring this policy is specifying an email address that will receive expiration/renewal notifications for any group that has no owner. This ensures that even orphaned groups—those without an owner to receive the standard renewal prompts—still generate an alert to the specified administrator address, satisfying the requirement to be notified when a team lacks an owner. Modifying Teams admin center settings, running Set-Team, or running Add-AzureADMSLifecyclePolicyGroup do not provide this owner-missing notification capability.

**Learn more:** [Set expiration for Microsoft 365 groups - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-lifecycle) · [Group expiration policy quickstart - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-quickstart-expiration)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
Users report that their presence information is available to external partners.  
  
You need to ensure that the presence information is available only to the external partners on the users' contact lists.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, add the external partners to the Allow only specific external domains list.
From External collaboration settings in the Azure Active Directory admin center, configure Guest user access restrictions.

questions.explanation: Advanced privacy mode (Set-CsPrivacyConfiguration -EnablePrivacyMode $true) restricts presence information visibility to only users on the recipient's contact list. This prevents external partners from seeing presence details unless they have been explicitly added as contacts, providing granular control over presence information disclosure while maintaining external communication capabilities.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Case study -  

This is a case study. Case studies are not timed separately. You can use as much exam time as you would like to complete each case. However, there may be additional case studies and sections on this exam. You must manage your time to ensure that you are able to complete all questions included on this exam in the time provided.  
  
To answer the questions included in a case study, you will need to reference information that is provided in the case study. Case studies might contain exhibits and other resources that provide more information about the scenario that is described in the case study. Each question is independent of the other questions in this case study.  
  
At the end of this case study, a review screen will appear. This screen allows you to review your answers and to make changes before you move to the next section of the exam. After you begin a new section, you cannot return to this section.  
  
To start the case study -  

To display the first question in this case study, click the Next button. Use the buttons in the left pane to explore the content of the case study before you answer the questions. Clicking these buttons displays information such as business requirements, existing environment, and problem statements. If the case study has an All Information tab, note that the information displayed is identical to the information displayed on the subsequent tabs. When you are ready to answer a question, click the Question button to return to the question.  
  
General Overview -  
  
Wingtip Toys is a manufacturing company that has 5,000 users, and locations across North America and Europe.  
  
Departments -  
  
The company has the following departments:  
  
• IT  

• Sales  

• Security  

• Customer support  

• Human resources (HR)  

• Research and development (R&D)  
  
Microsoft Office 365 Environment  
  
All users are assigned a Microsoft 365 E5 license and are enabled for Microsoft Teams Phone.  
  
Users in the R&D department are assigned a Teams Premium license.  
  
Requirements -  
  
Call Handling Requirements -  
  
Wingtip Toys identifies the following call handling requirements:  
  
• Inbound calls to the main telephone number of Wingtip Toys must be routed to the correct department by using an auto attendant.  

• During holiday periods, the auto attendant must perform the following actions:  

• Route customer support calls to the customer support department.  

• Play a recorded message for calls to all the other departments, and then disconnect the call.  
  
Meeting Requirements -  
  
Wingtip Toys identifies the following meeting requirements:  
  
• Meetings that include users from the R&D department must have a watermark applied to screen sharing sessions.  

• Once a quarter, the CEO of Wingtip Toys must host a live, online event that is attended by all users.  
  
Governance Requirements -  
  
Wingtip Toys identifies the following governance requirements:  
  
• New teams must meet the following requirements:  

• The Team type setting must be set to Private.  

• Users must be able to send emails to team channels.  

• Team members must be prevented from deleting messages from team channels.  

• Each team name must be validated against a list of blocked team names.  

• Each team name must contain a prefix of GRP and the department name as a suffix.  

• Team channels must include a pinned tab that displays the Wingtip Toys website.  

• When a user creates a team, the team picture must be the logo of the user's department.  

• The department manager of the user that creates the team must be assigned the Owner role for the team.  

• The use of animated GIFs must be prevented in team channels.  
  
Collaboration Requirements -  
  
Wingtip Toys identifies the following collaboration requirements:  
  
• Fabrikam users must be able to join team channels hosted by Wingtip Toys.  

• Wingtip Toys users must be prevented from joining team channels hosted by Fabrikam.  
  
Monitoring Requirements -  
  
A notification must be sent to users in the IT department when a Teams Rooms system goes offline.  
  
Pilot Project Requirements -  
  
Wingtip Toys is currently evaluating third-party call center apps that integrate with Teams. The security department mandates that all third-party apps be reviewed by a qualified analyst and comply with industry-standard frameworks.  
  
User Issues -  
  
Wingtip Toys users report audio and video issues when accessing Teams meetings by using a web browser.  
  
Business Requirements -  
  
Wingtip Toys identifies the following business requirements:  
  
• Follow the principle of least privilege.  

• Minimize administrative effort.  

• Minimize costs.  
  
Which governance requirement is met by using a team template?

options.text: The Team name must contain a GRP prefix.
Team channels must include a pinned tab that displays the Wingtip Toys website.
The Owner role for a team must be assigned to the department manager of the user that created the team.
Team members must be prevented from deleting messages from team channels.

questions.explanation: A team template predefines the channels, tabs, and apps that are provisioned when a team is created from it, so it can satisfy the requirement that team channels include a pinned tab displaying the company website. Naming prefixes/suffixes and blocked-name validation are enforced by a team naming policy, message-deletion restrictions by a messaging policy, and owner assignment by a separate provisioning process (e.g., Graph/PowerShell automation), none of which are configured through a team template.

You have a Microsoft 365 subscription named contoso.com that uses Microsoft Teams.  
  
You need to ensure that Microsoft Teams users can perform the following tasks:  
  
• Search for customers that use Skype (Consumer).  

• Start a Skype chat with the customers.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: From the Microsoft Teams admin center, turn on guest access.
From the Microsoft Teams admin center, turn on external access.
Add a _sipfederationtls SRV record to the contoso.com DNS domain.
Add a _sipinternaltls SRV record to the contoso.com DNS domain.
From the Azure portal, configure Azure AD B2C.

questions.explanation: To enable Teams users to communicate with Skype consumers, external access must be enabled in the Microsoft Teams admin center. Additionally, the _sipfederationtls SRV record must be added to DNS to allow Skype consumers to discover and connect to your organization's domain. Together, these changes establish the federation connectivity required for Skype consumer interoperability.
